sentences.zh: ◎回鶻上

translations.literal: ◎ Uyghurs, Part One
translations.idiomatic: ◎ The Uyghurs (Part One)

sentences.zh: 回紇，其先匈奴也，俗多乘高輪車，元魏時亦號高車部，或曰敕勒，訛為鐵勒。

translations.literal: The Huihe were originally of Xiongnu stock; their custom was to ride much in high-wheeled carts. Under the Northern Wei they were also called the Gaoche tribes, or the Chile; corrupted, this became Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe traced their origins to the Xiongnu. They commonly traveled in high-wheeled carts. Under the Northern Wei they were also known as the Gaoche tribes, or as the Chile—a name later corrupted to Tiele.

sentences.zh: 其部落曰袁紇、薛延陀、契羽、都播、骨利幹、多覽葛、仆骨、拔野古、同羅、渾、思結、斛薛、奚結、阿跌、白霫，凡十有五種，皆散處磧北。

translations.literal: Their tribes were called Yuanhe, Xueyantuo, Qiyu, Dubo, Guligan, Duolange, Pugu, Bayegu, Tongluo, Hun, Sijie, Huxue, Xijie, Adie, and Baixi—fifteen kinds in all—each scattered north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribal groups included the Yuanhe, Xueyantuo, Qiyu, Dubo, Guligan, Duolange, Pugu, Bayegu, Tongluo, Hun, Sijie, Huxue, Xijie, Adie, and Baixi—fifteen in all—scattered across the lands north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 袁紇者，亦曰烏護，曰烏紇，至隋曰韋紇。

translations.literal: The Yuanhe were also called Wuhu, also called Wuhe; under the Sui they were called Weihe.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanhe were also known as the Wuhu and the Wuhe; under the Sui dynasty they were called the Weihe.

sentences.zh: 其人驍強，初無酋長，逐水草轉徙，善騎射，喜盜鈔，臣於突厥，突厥資其財力雄北荒。

translations.literal: These people were fierce and strong; at first they had no chieftain, moving with water and grass, skilled at mounted archery and fond of raiding. They submitted to the Turks, who relied on their wealth and strength to dominate the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: They were a fierce people who at first had no single chief, roaming with pasture and water. They excelled at mounted archery and delighted in plunder. They submitted to the Turks, who drew on their wealth and fighting power to dominate the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 大業中，處羅可汗攻脅鐵勒部，裒責其財，既又恐其怨，則集渠豪數百悉坑之，韋紇乃並仆骨、同羅、拔野古叛去，自為俟斤，稱回紇。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, Qaghan Chuluo attacked and coerced the Tiele tribes, stripping them of their wealth; then, fearing their resentment, he gathered several hundred tribal magnates and buried them all alive. The Weihe thereupon joined Pugu, Tongluo, and Bayegu in rebellion, made themselves irkin, and took the name Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign, Qaghan Chuluo attacked the Tiele and extorted their wealth. Fearing their resentment afterward, he summoned several hundred tribal leaders and had them all buried alive. The Weihe then rose with the Pugu, Tongluo, and Bayegu, set up their own irkin, and called themselves the Huihe.

sentences.zh: 回紇姓藥羅葛氏，居薛延陀北娑陵水上，距京師七千里。

translations.literal: The Huihe bore the surname Yaglakar and dwelt on the Selenga River north of the Xueyantuo, seven thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe clan was the Yaglakar. They lived on the Selenga River north of the Xueyantuo, seven thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 眾十萬，勝兵半之。

translations.literal: Their population was one hundred thousand; fit warriors were half that number.
translations.idiomatic: They numbered one hundred thousand people, with half that many men fit for war.

sentences.zh: 地磧鹵，畜多大足羊。

translations.literal: The land was saline and barren; their livestock were mostly large-hoofed sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The land was salty and poor, and they raised mostly fat-tailed sheep.

sentences.zh: 有時健俟斤者，眾始推為君長。

translations.literal: There was one Shijian irkin, whom the masses first acclaimed as paramount chief.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Shijian irkin was the first whom the people acclaimed as their paramount leader.

sentences.zh: 子曰菩薩，材勇有謀，嗜獵射，戰必身先，所向輒摧破，故下皆畏附，為時健所逐。

translations.literal: His son was called Pusa: talented, brave, and resourceful, devoted to hunting and archery. In battle he always led from the front; wherever he turned, the enemy was shattered. Therefore all below feared him and attached themselves to him, and Shijian drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: His son was named Pusa—a man of talent, courage, and cunning who loved the hunt and the bow. In battle he always charged ahead, and wherever he struck the foe broke. All the tribes feared and followed him, until Shijian drove him into exile.

sentences.zh: 時健死，部人賢菩薩，立之。

translations.literal: When Shijian died, the tribesmen deemed Pusa worthy and enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: After Shijian died, the tribes judged Pusa worthy and set him up as their leader.

sentences.zh: 母曰烏羅渾，性嚴明，能決平部事。

translations.literal: His mother was called Wuluohun; stern and clear-minded by nature, she could settle and pacify tribal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Wuluohun was stern and discerning, and could judge and settle disputes throughout the tribe.

sentences.zh: 回紇繇是浸盛。

translations.literal: From this the Huihe gradually grew mighty.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the Huihe grew steadily stronger.

sentences.zh: 與薛延陀共攻突厥北邊，頡利遣欲谷設領騎十萬討之，菩薩身將五千騎破之馬鬛山，追北至天山，大俘其部人，聲震北方。

translations.literal: Together with the Xueyantuo they attacked the Turks' northern frontier. Jieli sent the yabgu she with one hundred thousand horsemen to punish them. Pusa himself led five thousand riders and defeated them at Mount Mane; pursuing north to the Heavenly Mountains, he took a great captivity of tribesmen, and his fame shook the north.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Xueyantuo in raiding the Turks' northern marches. Jieli sent the yabgu she at the head of one hundred thousand horsemen against them. Pusa personally led five thousand cavalry, routed them at Mount Mane, and pursued north to the Heavenly Mountains, taking vast numbers prisoner. His renown thundered across the north.

sentences.zh: 繇是附薛延陀，相唇齒，號活頡利發，樹牙獨樂水上。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attached himself to the Xueyantuo as lip and teeth, took the title Huotelifa, and planted his royal camp on the Duluo River.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied with the Xueyantuo as mutual shield and sword, took the title Huotelifa, and pitched his royal camp on the Duluo River.

sentences.zh: ，始來朝，獻方物。

translations.literal: They then first came to court and presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: They came to court for the first time and presented tribute goods from their land.

sentences.zh: 突厥已亡，惟回紇與薛延陀為最雄強。

translations.literal: The Turks were already destroyed; only the Huihe and the Xueyantuo were the most powerful.
translations.idiomatic: With the Turks gone, only the Huihe and the Xueyantuo remained the strongest powers of the steppe.

sentences.zh: 菩薩死，其酋胡祿俟利發吐迷度與諸部攻薛延陀，殘之，並有其地，遂南逾賀蘭山，境諸河。

translations.literal: When Pusa died, their chief Hulusili fa Tumidu with the various tribes attacked the Xueyantuo, shattered them, and seized their lands. They then crossed south over the Helan Mountains and bordered the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: After Pusa died, the tribal chief Tumidu, Hulusili fa, led the tribes against the Xueyantuo, broke their power, and took their territory. They then crossed the Helan Mountains to the south and reached the banks of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 遣使者獻款，太宗為幸靈州，次涇陽，受其功。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to offer allegiance. Emperor Taizong, for his sake, visited Lingzhou and halted at Jingyang to receive his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to pledge allegiance. Emperor Taizong traveled to Lingzhou for his sake and stopped at Jingyang to honor his service.

sentences.zh: 於是鐵勒十一部皆來言：「延陀不事大國，以自取亡，其下麕駭鳥散，不知所之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the eleven Tiele tribes all came saying: "The Xueyantuo would not serve the great state and brought ruin on themselves; their followers scattered like startled deer and birds, not knowing where they went.
translations.idiomatic: Then the eleven Tiele tribes all came forward and said, "The Xueyantuo refused to serve the great empire and destroyed themselves. Their people fled like frightened deer and scattered birds, with no one knowing where they had gone.

sentences.zh: 今各有分地，願歸命天子，請置唐官。」

translations.literal: Now each has its allotted territory; we wish to submit our lives to the Son of Heaven and ask that Tang officials be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Now each of us holds his own territory. We wish to submit to the Son of Heaven and ask that Tang officials be appointed over us.

sentences.zh: 有詔張飲高會，引見渠長等，以唐官官之，凡數千人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a great feast spread; the canal chiefs and others were led in audience and given Tang offices—several thousand men in all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for a grand banquet. The tribal chiefs were presented in audience and invested with Tang offices—several thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 明年復入朝。

translations.literal: The next year they again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they came to court again.

sentences.zh: 乃以回紇部為瀚海，多覽葛部為燕然，仆骨部為金微，拔野古部為幽陵，同羅部為龜林，思結部為盧山，皆號都督府；

translations.literal: The Huihe tribe was made Hanhai, the Duolange tribe Yanshan, the Pugu tribe Jinwei, the Bayegu tribe Youling, the Tongluo tribe Guilin, and the Sijie tribe Lushan—all styled protectorates;
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe were made the Hanhai protectorate, the Duolange Yanshan, the Pugu Jinwei, the Bayegu Youling, the Tongluo Guilin, and the Sijie Lushan—each styled a protectorate;

sentences.zh: 以渾為臯蘭州，斛薛為高闕州，阿跌為雞田州，契羽為榆溪州，奚結為雞鹿州，思結別部為蹛林州，白霫為窴顏州；

translations.literal: the Hun were made Gaolan prefecture, the Huxue Gaoque prefecture, the Adie Jitian prefecture, the Qiyu Yuxi prefecture, the Xijie Jilu prefecture, a separate Sijie division Dailin prefecture, and the Baixi Tuyan prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: the Hun became Gaolan prefecture, the Huxue Gaoque, the Adie Jitian, the Qiyu Yuxi, the Xijie Jilu, a separate Sijie branch Dailin, and the Baixi Tuyan;

sentences.zh: 其西北結骨部為堅昆府，北骨利幹為玄闕州，東北俱羅勃為燭龍州；

translations.literal: to the northwest the Jiegu tribe was made Jiankun prefecture, to the north Guligan Xuanque prefecture, and to the northeast Jurubo Zhulong prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: to the northwest the Jiegu were made Jiankun prefecture, to the north Guligan Xuanque, and to the northeast Jurubo Zhulong;

sentences.zh: 皆以酋領為都督、刺史、長史、司馬，即故單于臺置燕然都護府統之，六都督、七州皆隸屬，以李素立為燕然都護。

translations.literal: in each case tribal leaders were made protectors, prefects, chief administrators, and aides. On the site of the old Chanyu Terrace the Yanshan Protectorate was established to govern them; the six protectorates and seven prefectures were all subordinate to it, and Li Suli was made Yanshan protector.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders were appointed protectors, prefects, chief administrators, and aides. On the site of the old Chanyu Terrace the Yanshan Protectorate was set up to govern them; all six protectorates and seven prefectures were placed under it, and Li Suli was named Yanshan protector.

sentences.zh: 其都督、刺史給玄金魚符，黃金為文，天子方招寵遠夷，作絳黃瑞錦文袍、寶刀、珍器賜之。

translations.literal: The protectors and prefects were given dark-gold fish tally tokens inscribed in gold. The Son of Heaven was then courting distant barbarians and made crimson-and-yellow brocade robes, precious swords, and rare vessels to bestow on them.
translations.idiomatic: Protectors and prefects received dark-gold fish tally tokens with gold inscriptions. The emperor was courting distant peoples and had crimson-and-yellow brocade robes, precious swords, and rare vessels made to bestow on them.

sentences.zh: 帝坐秘殿，陳十部樂，殿前設高坫，置朱提瓶其上，潛泉浮酒，自左閣通坫趾註之瓶，轉受百斛鐐盎，回紇數千人飲畢，尚不能半。

translations.literal: The emperor sat in the secret hall; the music of the ten tribes was arrayed. Before the hall a high altar was set up with a Zhuti vase upon it; a hidden spring buoyed up wine, which from the left gate flowed through the foot of the altar into the vase, then turned to fill a hundred-bushel cauldron. Several thousand Huihe drank their fill and still could not empty half of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat in the inner hall while the music of the ten tribes was performed. Before the hall stood a high altar bearing a Zhuti vase; wine rose from a hidden spring and flowed from the left gate through the base of the altar into the vase, then on into a hundred-bushel cauldron. Several thousand Huihe drank their fill and still could not finish half the wine.

sentences.zh: 又詔文武五品官以上祖飲尚書省中。

translations.literal: He also ordered civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above to host a farewell feast for them in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above to host a farewell banquet for them at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 渠領共言：「生荒陋地，歸身聖化，天至尊賜官爵，與為百姓，依唐若父母然。

translations.literal: The canal leaders together said: "Born in a crude and remote land, we have submitted to holy transformation. The Heaven-Supreme One has granted us offices and ranks and made us his people; we rely on Tang as on father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs said together, "We were born in a crude and distant land, but we have submitted to your holy rule. The Heaven-Supreme One has granted us offices and made us his people. We rely on Tang as children rely on their parents.

sentences.zh: 請於回紇、突厥部治大塗，號『參天至尊道』，世為唐臣。」

translations.literal: We ask that between the Huihe and Turk lands a great road be built, called the 'Way of the Heaven-Reaching Supreme One,' and that we be Tang subjects for all generations."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that a great road be built between Huihe and Turk lands, called the Way of the Heaven-Reaching Supreme One, and that we remain subjects of Tang for all generations.

sentences.zh: 乃詔磧南鸊鵜泉之陽置過郵六十八所，具群馬、湩、肉待使客，歲內貂皮為賦。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered sixty-eight relay stations set up south of the desert on the sunny side of the Pipi Spring, stocked with herds of horses, kumiss, and meat to receive envoys; sable pelts were taken as annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then established sixty-eight relay stations south of the desert on the sunny side of Pipi Spring, stocked with herds, kumiss, and meat for traveling envoys. Sable pelts were levied as annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 乃拜吐迷度為懷化大將軍、瀚海都督；

translations.literal: Tumidu was then appointed General Who Cherishes Transformation and Hanhai Protector;
translations.idiomatic: Tumidu was appointed General Who Cherishes Transformation and Hanhai Protector;

sentences.zh: 然私自號可汗，署官吏，壹似突厥，有外宰相六、內宰相三，又有都督、將軍、司馬之號。

translations.literal: yet privately he styled himself qaghan, appointed officials, and modeled everything on the Turks, with six outer chancellors, three inner chancellors, and also the titles of protector, general, and aide.
translations.idiomatic: yet privately he styled himself qaghan, appointed officials, and organized his state on the Turkish model, with six outer chancellors, three inner chancellors, and the ranks of protector, general, and aide.

sentences.zh: 帝更詔時健俟斤它部為祁連州，隸靈州都督，白霫它部為居延州。

translations.literal: The emperor further ordered Shijian irkin's other tribes made Qilian prefecture, subordinate to the Lingzhou protector, and the Baixi's other tribes made Juyan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further made Shijian irkin's other tribes into Qilian prefecture under the Lingzhou protector, and the Baixi's other tribes into Juyan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吐迷度兄子烏紇烝吐迷度之妻，遂與俱陸莫賀達干俱羅勃謀亂而歸車鼻可汗，二人者皆車鼻婿，故烏紇領騎夜劫吐迷度殺之。

translations.literal: Tumidu's nephew Wuhe took Tumidu's wife in marriage. He then plotted rebellion with Julu mohada Jurubo to return to Qaghan Chebi; both men were sons-in-law of Chebi, so Wuhe led horsemen by night, seized Tumidu, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tumidu's nephew Wuhe married Tumidu's widow. He then plotted rebellion with Jurubo, Julu mohada, intending to return to Qaghan Chebi. Both men were Chebi's sons-in-law, so Wuhe led horsemen by night, seized Tumidu, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 燕然副都護元禮臣遣使紿烏紇，許白為都督，烏紇不疑，即往謝，因斬以徇。

translations.literal: Yanshan vice-protector Yuan Lichen sent an envoy to deceive Wuhe, promising to clear him and make him protector. Wuhe did not doubt this, went at once to give thanks, and was beheaded as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lichen, vice-protector of Yanshan, sent an envoy to deceive Wuhe, promising to clear his name and make him protector. Wuhe believed him, came at once to give thanks, and was beheaded as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 帝恐諸部攜解，命兵部尚書崔敦禮持節臨撫，贈吐迷度左衛大將軍，賻祭備厚，擢其子婆閏左驍衛大將軍，襲父所領。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing the tribes would waver and scatter, ordered Minister of War Cui Dunli to go with credentials to reassure them. He posthumously gave Tumidu the title of Left Guard General and furnished lavish funeral gifts; his son Porun was promoted to Left Valiant Cavalry General and inherited his father's command.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the tribes would break apart, the emperor sent Minister of War Cui Dunli with credentials to reassure them. He posthumously honored Tumidu as Left Guard General with lavish funeral gifts, and promoted his son Porun to Left Valiant Cavalry General to inherit his father's command.

sentences.zh: 俱羅勃既入朝，帝不遣。

translations.literal: Jurubo had already come to court, and the emperor would not let him leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jurubo had come to court, and the emperor would not allow him to return home.

sentences.zh: 阿史那賀魯之盜北庭，婆閏以騎五萬助契何力等破賀魯，收北庭；

translations.literal: When Ashina Helu raided Beiting, Porun with fifty thousand horsemen aided Qibi Heli and others in defeating Helu and recovering Beiting;
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina Helu raided Beiting, Porun led fifty thousand horsemen to help Qibi Heli and others defeat Helu and recover Beiting;

sentences.zh: 又從伊麗道行軍總管任雅相等再破賀魯金牙山，遷右衛大將軍，從討高麗有功。

translations.literal: he again followed campaign commander-in-chief of the Yili route Ren Yaqiang and others in a second defeat of Helu at Golden Tooth Mountain, was transferred to Right Guard General, and followed the campaign against Koguryŏ with merit.
translations.idiomatic: he again followed Ren Yaqiang, campaign commander of the Yili route, in a second defeat of Helu at Golden Tooth Mountain, was promoted to Right Guard General, and served with merit in the campaign against Koguryŏ.

sentences.zh: 婆閏死，子比栗嗣。

translations.literal: When Porun died, his son Bili succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Porun died, his son Bili succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，以燕然都護府領回紇，更號瀚海都護府，以磧為限，大抵北諸蕃悉隸之。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo era the Yanshan Protectorate, which governed the Huihe, was renamed the Hanhai Protectorate; with the desert as its limit, nearly all northern tribes were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longshuo era the Yanshan Protectorate governing the Huihe was renamed the Hanhai Protectorate. With the desert as its boundary, nearly all northern tribes fell under its authority.

sentences.zh: 比栗死，子獨解支嗣。

translations.literal: When Bili died, his son Dujiezhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Bili died, his son Dujiezhi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 武后時，突厥默啜方強，取鐵勒故地，故回紇與契、思結、渾三部度磧，徙甘、涼間，然唐常取其壯騎佐赤水軍云。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu the Turk Mo-ch'o was then strong and seized the old Tiele lands, so the Huihe with the Qi, Sijie, and Hun tribes crossed the desert and moved between Gan and Liang; yet Tang often took their strong horsemen to assist the Chishui army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu the Turk Mo-ch'o was strong and seized the old Tiele lands. The Huihe therefore crossed the desert with the Qi, Sijie, and Hun tribes and settled between Gan and Liang. Even so, Tang often drafted their strongest horsemen to serve in the Chishui army.

sentences.zh: 獨解支死，子伏帝匐立。

translations.literal: When Dujiezhi died, his son Fudifu was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: When Dujiezhi died, his son Fudifu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 明年，助唐攻殺默啜，於是別部移健頡利發與同羅、霫等皆來，詔置其部於大武軍北。

translations.literal: The next year they aided Tang in attacking and killing Mo-ch'o. Thereupon the separate tribes Yijian telifa with the Tongluo, Xi, and others all came; an edict settled their tribes north of the Dawu army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they helped Tang attack and kill Mo-ch'o. Then the separate tribes led by Yijian telifa, together with the Tongluo, Xi, and others, all came in. An edict settled their people north of the Dawu army.

sentences.zh: 伏帝匐死，子承宗立，涼州都督王君㚟誣暴其罪，流死州。

translations.literal: When Fudifu died, his son Chengzong was enthroned. Liangzhou protector Wang Junlie falsely charged him with violent crimes and had him exiled to die in a distant prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Fudifu died, his son Chengzong succeeded. Wang Junlie, protector of Liangzhou, falsely accused him of violent crimes and had him exiled to a distant prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 當此時，回紇稍不循，族子瀚海府司馬護輸乘眾怨，共殺君㚟，梗絕安西諸國朝貢道。

translations.literal: At this time the Huihe were somewhat unruly. A clansman, Hanhai prefecture aide Hu-lu, seized on popular resentment and together they killed Junlie, blocking the tribute road of the Anxi states.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Huihe had grown restive. A clansman named Hu-lu, aide of the Hanhai prefecture, seized on popular anger and joined in killing Junlie, cutting off the tribute route of the Anxi states.

sentences.zh: 久之，奔突厥，死。

translations.literal: After a long while he fled to the Turks and died.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he fled to the Turks and died there.

sentences.zh: 子骨力裴羅立。

translations.literal: His son Gulipeiluo was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gulipeiluo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 會突厥亂，天寶初，裴羅與葛邏祿自稱左右葉護，助拔悉蜜擊走烏蘇可汗。

translations.literal: It happened that the Turks were in turmoil. At the beginning of the Tianbao era Peiluo and the Qarlugs styled themselves left and right yabghu and helped the Basmyls drive off Qaghan Wusu.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks fell into turmoil. At the start of the Tianbao era Peiluo and the Qarlugs styled themselves left and right yabghu and helped the Basmyls drive off Qaghan Wusu.

sentences.zh: 後三年，襲破拔悉蜜，斬頡跌伊施可汗，遣使上狀，自稱骨咄祿毗伽闕可汗，天子以為奉義王，南居突厥故地，徙牙烏德山、昆河之間，南距西城千七百里，西城，漢高闕塞也，北盡磧口三百里，悉有九姓地。

translations.literal: Three years later he raided and broke the Basmyls, beheaded Qaghan Yiedie Yishi, and sent envoys to report upward. He styled himself Qutluq Bilge Kül Qaghan; the Son of Heaven made him Prince Who Upholds Righteousness. He moved south to the old Turk lands, shifting his royal camp between Mount Wude and the Kun River—one thousand seven hundred li south of the Western City, which was the Han Gaoque Pass—north to the desert mouth three hundred li, holding all the lands of the Nine Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he overran the Basmyls, beheaded Qaghan Yiedie Yishi, and sent envoys to report his victory. He styled himself Qutluq Bilge Kül Qaghan, and the emperor made him Prince Who Upholds Righteousness. He moved south into the old Turk lands and pitched his camp between Mount Wude and the Kun River—one thousand seven hundred li south of the Western City, the Han Gaoque Pass—with the desert mouth three hundred li to the north, holding all the territory of the Nine Surnames.

sentences.zh: 九姓者，曰藥羅葛，曰胡咄葛，曰啒羅勿，曰貊歌息訖，曰阿勿嘀，曰葛薩，曰斛嗢素，曰藥勿葛，曰奚牙勿。

translations.literal: The Nine Surnames were: Yaglakar, Huduoge, Waluowu, Mogexiqi, Awudi, Gesa, Huwasu, Yaowuge, and Xiyawu.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Surnames were the Yaglakar, Huduoge, Waluowu, Mogexiqi, Awudi, Gesa, Huwasu, Yaowuge, and Xiyawu.

sentences.zh: 藥羅葛，回紇姓也，與仆骨、渾、拔、野古、同羅、思結、契六種相等夷，不列於數，後破有拔悉蜜、葛邏祿，總十一姓，並置都督，號十一部落。

translations.literal: Yaglakar was the Huihe surname. With the six kinds Pugu, Hun, Bayegu, Tongluo, Sijie, and Qi they were equal and not counted in the number. Later, after defeating the Basmyls and Qarlugs, there were eleven surnames in all; protectors were appointed for each, and they were called the Eleven Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yaglakar was the Huihe clan name. Together with the six tribes Pugu, Hun, Bayegu, Tongluo, Sijie, and Qi they stood as equals and were not counted among the nine. Later, after the defeat of the Basmyls and Qarlugs, there were eleven surnames in all; each was given a protector, and they were called the Eleven Tribes.

sentences.zh: 自是，戰常以二客部為先鋒。

translations.literal: From this time in battle they regularly used the two guest tribes as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they regularly used the two guest tribes as their vanguard in battle.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜為骨咄祿毗伽闕懷仁可汗，前殿列仗，中書令內案授冊使者，使者出門升輅，至皇城門，降乘馬，幡節導以行。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Qutluq Bilge Kül Qaghan Who Cherishes Benevolence. In the front hall arms were arrayed; the chief minister at the inner desk invested the envoy with the patent. The envoy left the gate, mounted the carriage, reached the imperial city gate, dismounted to take horse, and banners and insignia led him on.
translations.idiomatic: An edict invested him as Qutluq Bilge Kül Qaghan Who Cherishes Benevolence. Arms were arrayed in the front hall; the chief minister at the inner desk handed the patent to the envoy. The envoy left the gate, mounted his carriage, reached the imperial city gate, dismounted for a horse, and proceeded under banners and insignia.

sentences.zh: 凡冊可汗，率用此禮。

translations.literal: Whenever a qaghan was invested, this ceremony was generally used.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture of a qaghan generally followed this ceremony.

sentences.zh: 明年，裴羅又攻殺突厥白眉可汗，遣頓啜羅達干來上功，拜裴羅左驍衛員外大將軍，斥地愈廣，東極室韋，西金山，南控大漠，盡得古匈奴地。

translations.literal: The next year Peiluo again attacked and killed the Turk White-Brow Qaghan and sent Dunduoluodagan to report the merit. Peiluo was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry Supernumerary General. His territory grew ever wider: east to the Shiwei, west to the Golden Mountains, south controlling the great desert—he held all the old Xiongnu lands.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Peiluo again attacked and killed the Turk White-Brow Qaghan and sent Dunduoluodagan to report his victory. Peiluo was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry Supernumerary General. His domain grew ever wider: east to the Shiwei, west to the Golden Mountains, south across the great desert—he held all the old Xiongnu lands.

sentences.zh: 裴羅死，子磨延啜立，號葛勒可汗，剽悍善用兵，歲遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: When Peiluo died, his son Moyanchuo was enthroned, styled Qaghan Gele. Fierce and skilled in war, he sent envoys to court every year.
translations.idiomatic: When Peiluo died, his son Moyanchuo succeeded, styled Qaghan Gele. Fierce and skilled in war, he sent envoys to court every year.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，使者來請助討祿山，帝詔敦煌郡王承寀與約，而令仆固懷恩送王，因召其兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, envoys came asking aid against Lushan. The emperor ordered Prince of Dunhuang Chengcai to make the pact and commanded Pugu Huai'en to escort the prince and thereby summon their troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, envoys came asking help against Lushan. The emperor ordered Prince of Dunhuang Chengcai to negotiate the alliance and sent Pugu Huai'en to escort the prince and summon Huihe troops.

sentences.zh: 可汗喜，以可敦妹為女，妻承寀，遣渠領來請和親，帝欲固其心，即封虜女為毗伽公主。

translations.literal: The qaghan rejoiced, took his khatun's younger sister as a daughter, and gave her in marriage to Chengcai. He sent canal leaders to request a marriage alliance. The emperor, wishing to bind his heart, at once ennobled a palace woman as Princess Pijia.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan rejoiced, adopted his khatun's younger sister as a daughter, and gave her to Chengcai in marriage. He sent tribal leaders to request a marriage alliance. Wishing to secure his loyalty, the emperor ennobled a palace woman as Princess Pijia.

sentences.zh: 於是可汗自將，與朔方節度使郭子儀合討同羅諸蕃，破之河上。

translations.literal: Thereupon the qaghan led the army in person and, together with Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi, jointly attacked the Tongluo and various tribes, defeating them on the river.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan then led his army in person and, together with Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, attacked the Tongluo and other tribes, defeating them on the river.

sentences.zh: 與子儀會呼延谷，可汗恃其強，陳兵引子儀拜狼纛而後見。

translations.literal: He met Ziyi at Huyan Valley. The qaghan, relying on his strength, arrayed troops and made Ziyi bow to the wolf banner before granting him audience.
translations.idiomatic: He met Ziyi at Huyan Valley. Trusting in his strength, the qaghan drew up his troops and made Ziyi bow to the wolf banner before he would receive him.

sentences.zh: 帝駐彭原，使者葛羅支見，恥班下，帝不欲使鞅鞅，引升殿，慰而遣。

translations.literal: The emperor was stationed at Pengyuan. The envoy Geluozhi came to audience and was ashamed to stand below the ranks. The emperor, not wishing him to leave discontented, led him up to the hall, comforted him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Pengyuan. Envoy Geluozhi came to audience, ashamed to stand below the court ranks. Not wishing him to leave offended, the emperor brought him up to the hall, comforted him, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 俄以大將軍多攬等造朝，及太子葉護身將四千騎來，惟所命。

translations.literal: Soon the great general Duolan and others came to court, and the heir Yehu personally led four thousand riders to come, ready for whatever was commanded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the great general Duolan and others came to court, and the heir Yehu personally led four thousand horsemen, ready to obey whatever command was given.

sentences.zh: 帝因冊毗伽公主為王妃，擢承寀宗正卿；

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon invested Princess Pijia as royal consort and promoted Chengcai to Director of the Imperial Clan;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then invested Princess Pijia as royal consort and promoted Chengcai to Director of the Imperial Clan;

sentences.zh: 可汗亦封承寀為葉護，給四節，令與其葉護共將。

translations.literal: the qaghan also enfeoffed Chengcai as yabghu, granted him the four seasonal gifts, and ordered him to command jointly with his own yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: the qaghan also enfeoffed Chengcai as yabghu, granted him the four seasonal gifts, and ordered him to command jointly with his own yabghu.

sentences.zh: 帝命廣平王見葉護，約為昆弟，葉護大喜，使首領達干等先到扶風見子儀，子儀犒飲三日。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Prince of Guangping to meet Yehu and covenant as sworn brothers. Yehu was greatly pleased and sent chief leaders Dagan and others ahead to Fufeng to see Ziyi; Ziyi feasted and entertained them for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Prince of Guangping to meet Yehu and swear brotherhood with him. Yehu was overjoyed and sent chief leaders including Dagan ahead to Fufeng to see Ziyi, who feasted them for three days.

sentences.zh: 葉護辭曰：「國多難，我助討逆，何敢食！」

translations.literal: Yehu declined, saying: "The state is in great difficulty; I have come to help punish the rebels—how dare I feast!
translations.idiomatic: Yehu declined, saying, "The empire is in grave trouble. I have come to help put down the rebels—how can I feast!

sentences.zh: 固命，乃留。

translations.literal: They pressed him firmly, and only then did he stay.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him until he agreed to stay.

sentences.zh: 既行，日賜牛四十角、羊八百蹄、米四十斛。

translations.literal: Once they marched, each day they were given forty horns of cattle, eight hundred hooves of sheep, and forty bushels of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Once they marched, they were supplied each day with forty head of cattle, eight hundred sheep, and forty bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 香積之戰，陣澧上，賊詭伏騎於王師左，將襲我，仆固懷恩麾回紇馳之，盡翦其伏，乃出賊背，與鎮西、北庭節度使李嗣業夾之，賊大敗，進收長安。

translations.literal: At the battle of Xiangji they formed battle lines on the Li. The rebels hid cavalry in ambush on the left of the imperial army, intending to strike us. Pugu Huai'en commanded the Huihe to charge them and utterly cut down the ambush. They then came out behind the rebels and, with Li Siye, military commissioner of Zhenxi and Beiting, attacked from both sides. The rebels were greatly defeated, and the army advanced to recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Xiangji the armies formed on the Li River. The rebels hid cavalry to the left of the imperial forces, ready to strike. Pugu Huai'en sent the Huihe charging in and wiped out the ambush. They then struck from behind while Li Siye, military commissioner of Zhenxi and Beiting, attacked from the front. The rebels were routed, and the army advanced to recover Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 懷恩率回紇、南蠻、大食眾繚都而南，壁浐東，進次陜西，戰新店。

translations.literal: Huai'en led the Huihe, southern barbarians, and Arab forces winding around the capital southward, encamped east of the Chan, advanced to camp at Shaanxi, and fought at Xindian.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en led the Huihe, southern tribes, and Arab forces south around the capital, encamped east of the Chan, advanced to Shaanxi, and fought at Xindian.

sentences.zh: 初，回紇至曲沃，葉護使將軍鼻施吐撥裴羅旁南山東出，搜賊伏谷中，殲之，營山陰。

translations.literal: At first, when the Huihe reached Quwo, Yehu sent General Bishi Tubo Peiluo east along the southern flank of the mountains to search out rebel ambushes in the valleys, annihilated them, and encamped on the northern slope.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huihe first reached Quwo, Yehu sent General Bishi Tubo Peiluo east along the southern mountains to hunt rebel ambushes in the valleys, destroyed them, and encamped on the northern slope.

sentences.zh: 子儀等與賊戰，傾軍逐北，亂而卻，回紇望見，即逾西嶺，曳旗趨賊，出其後，賊反顧，遂大潰，追奔數十里，人馬相騰蹂，死者不可計，收仗械如丘。

translations.literal: Ziyi and others fought the rebels, threw the whole army into pursuit northward, then fell into disorder and retreated. The Huihe saw this, at once crossed the western ridge, dragged their banners toward the rebels, and came out behind them. The rebels looked back and thereupon broke in great rout. The pursuit ran several tens of li; men and horses trampled one another, and the dead were beyond counting. Captured arms piled like hills.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi and his forces fought the rebels and threw the whole army into a northward pursuit, then fell into disorder and fell back. The Huihe saw this, crossed the western ridge at once, swept their banners toward the enemy, and struck from behind. The rebels looked back and broke in rout. The pursuit ran for miles; men and horses trampled one another, and the dead were beyond count. Captured weapons piled like hills.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊挾安慶緒棄東京北度河，回紇大掠東都三日，奸人導之，府庫窮殫，廣平王欲止不可，而耆老以繒錦萬匹賂回紇，止不剽。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang took An Qingxu and abandoned the Eastern Capital, crossing the river north. The Huihe plundered the Eastern Capital greatly for three days; villains guided them, and the treasuries were utterly emptied. The Prince of Guangping wished to stop them but could not; then the elders bribed the Huihe with ten thousand bolts of silk and brocade, and the plundering ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang took An Qingxu and abandoned the Eastern Capital, fleeing north across the river. The Huihe looted the Eastern Capital for three days while villains guided them, emptying the treasuries. The Prince of Guangping tried to stop them but could not, until the elders bribed the Huihe with ten thousand bolts of silk and brocade and the looting ceased.

sentences.zh: 葉護還京師，帝遣群臣勞之長樂，帝坐前殿，召葉護升階，席酋領於下，宴且勞之，人人賜錦繡繒器。

translations.literal: Yehu returned to the capital. The emperor sent the ministers to welcome him at Changle. The emperor sat in the front hall, summoned Yehu to ascend the steps, seated the tribal chiefs below, feasted and comforted them, and to each man gave brocade, silk, and fine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Yehu returned to the capital. The emperor sent ministers to welcome him at Changle. Sitting in the front hall, the emperor summoned Yehu to ascend the steps, seated the tribal chiefs below, feasted and honored them, and gave each man brocade, silk, and fine vessels.

sentences.zh: 葉護頓首言：「留兵沙苑，臣歸料馬，以收范陽，訖除殘盜。」

translations.literal: Yehu bowed his head and said: "Leave the troops at Shayuan; I shall return to gather horses and recover Fanyang, until the remaining bandits are utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yehu bowed low and said, "Leave the troops at Shayuan. I will return to gather horses and recover Fanyang, until every last rebel is destroyed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為朕竭義勇，成大事，卿等力也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You have exhausted your righteous valor for Us and accomplished a great deed—this is your strength."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have spent your righteous valor for me and accomplished a great deed. This victory is your doing."

sentences.zh: 詔進司空，爵忠義王，歲給絹二萬匹，使至朔方軍受賜。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to Grand Marshal and enfeoffed him as Prince of Loyal Righteousness, with twenty thousand bolts of silk given yearly, to be received when he reached the Shuofang army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to Grand Marshal and enfeoffed him as Prince of Loyal Righteousness, with an annual grant of twenty thousand bolts of silk to be received at the Shuofang army.

sentences.zh: ，回紇使者多彥阿波與黑衣大食酋閣之等俱朝，爭長，有司使異門並進。

translations.literal: The Huihe envoy Duoyan Abo and the chief of the Black-Robed Arabs, Yan Zhi, came to court together and disputed precedence; the authorities had them enter by separate gates at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe envoy Duoyan Abo and Yan Zhi, chief of the Black-Robed Arabs, came to court together and disputed precedence. The authorities had them enter by separate gates at the same time.

sentences.zh: 又使請昏，許之。

translations.literal: They again sent envoys requesting marriage, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They again sent envoys to request a marriage alliance, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝以幼女寧國公主下嫁，即冊磨延啜為英武威遠毗伽可汗，詔漢中郡王瑀攝御史大夫為冊命使，以宗子右司郎中巽兼御史中丞為禮會使，並以副瑀，尚書右僕射裴冕送諸境。

translations.literal: The emperor gave his young daughter Princess Ningguo in marriage below and at once invested Moyanchuo as Qaghan Yingwu Weiyuan Pijia. He ordered Prince of Hanzhong Yu, acting as censor-in-chief, to be investiture envoy, and a clansman, Right Department Director Xun, concurrently vice censor-in-chief, to be rites envoy—both as Yu's deputies—and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Mian to escort her to the border.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave his young daughter Princess Ningguo in marriage and invested Moyanchuo as Qaghan Yingwu Weiyuan Pijia. He appointed Prince of Hanzhong Yu, acting censor-in-chief, as investiture envoy, and clansman Xun of the Right Department, concurrently vice censor-in-chief, as rites envoy—both as Yu's deputies—with Right Vice Director Pei Mian escorting the princess to the border.

sentences.zh: 帝餞公主，因幸咸陽，數尉勉，主泣曰：「國方多事，死不恨。」

translations.literal: The emperor saw the princess off on her journey and, going on to visit Xianyang, repeatedly comforted and encouraged her. The princess wept and said: "The state is in great troubles; I do not regret death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the princess off and visited Xianyang, comforting her again and again. The princess wept and said, "The empire is in crisis. I do not regret dying for it.

sentences.zh: 瑀至虜，而可汗胡帽赭袍坐帳中，儀衛光嚴，引瑀立帳外，問曰：「王，天可汗何屬？」

translations.literal: When Yu reached the barbarians, the qaghan sat in his tent in a barbarian cap and crimson robe, his guards brilliant and stern. He had Yu stand outside the tent and asked: "Prince, to what kinship does the Heaven Qaghan belong?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu reached the qaghan's camp, the qaghan sat in his tent wearing a barbarian cap and crimson robe, his guards splendid and stern. He had Yu stand outside the tent and asked, "Prince, what is the Heaven Qaghan to you?"

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「從昆弟也。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "He is a younger cousin brother."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "He is a cousin brother."

sentences.zh: 時中人雷靈俊立瑀上，又問：「立王上者為誰？」

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Lei Lingjun stood above Yu, and the qaghan asked again: "Who is it that makes the prince stand above you?"
translations.idiomatic: At that moment the eunuch Lei Lingjun stood above Yu on a platform. The qaghan asked again, "Who is the man standing above you?"

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「中人也。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "A palace man."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "A palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 可汗曰：「中人奴爾，顧立郎上乎？」

translations.literal: The qaghan said: "Palace men are slaves—why should one stand above a gentleman?"
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan said, "Palace attendants are slaves. Why should one stand above a gentleman?"

sentences.zh: 靈俊趨下。

translations.literal: Lingjun hurried down.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjun hurried down at once.

sentences.zh: 於是引瑀入，瑀不拜，可汗曰：「見國君，禮無不拜。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Yu inside. Yu did not bow. The qaghan said: "When one sees a ruler of a state, in ritual there is none who does not bow.
translations.idiomatic: He then led Yu inside. Yu did not bow. The qaghan said, "When one meets a ruler of a state, custom requires a bow.

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「天子顧可汗有功，以愛女結好。

translations.literal: Yu said: "The Son of Heaven, mindful of the qaghan's merit, has joined in friendship through his beloved daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "The Son of Heaven, mindful of your merit, has joined our houses through his beloved daughter.

sentences.zh: 比中國與夷狄婚，皆宗室子。

translations.literal: When China marries with barbarians, it has always been with daughters of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: When China marries barbarian rulers, it has always been with daughters of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 今寧國乃帝玉女，有德容，萬里來降，可汗天子婿，當以禮見，安踞受詔邪？」

translations.literal: Now Ningguo is the emperor's jade daughter, with virtue and grace, who has come ten thousand li to descend in marriage. The qaghan is the Son of Heaven's son-in-law and ought to receive him with ritual courtesy—how can he sit sprawled and receive the patent?
translations.idiomatic: Princess Ningguo is the emperor's own daughter, virtuous and gracious, who has traveled ten thousand li to marry you. You are the Son of Heaven's son-in-law and ought to receive his envoy with courtesy. How can you sit sprawled and take the patent?

sentences.zh: 可汗慚，乃起奉詔，拜受冊。

translations.literal: The qaghan was ashamed, rose to receive the patent with both hands, and bowed to accept the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, the qaghan rose, received the patent with both hands, and bowed to accept the investiture.

sentences.zh: 翌日，尊主為可敦。

translations.literal: The next day he honored the princess as khatun.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he honored the princess as khatun.

sentences.zh: 瑀所賫賜物，可汗盡與其牙下酋領。

translations.literal: The gifts that Yu had brought, the qaghan gave entirely to the tribal chiefs under his royal camp.
translations.idiomatic: The gifts Yu had brought, the qaghan gave in full to the tribal chiefs of his royal camp.

sentences.zh: 瑀還，獻馬五百匹、貂裘、白氈等。

translations.literal: Yu returned and presented five hundred horses, sable furs, white felts, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu returned, he presented five hundred horses, sable furs, white felts, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 乃使王子骨啜特勒、宰相帝德等率騎三千助討賊，帝因命仆固懷恩總之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent the prince Guchuo tegin, the chancellor Dide, and others to lead three thousand horsemen to help attack the rebels, and the emperor thereupon ordered Pugu Huai'en to command them overall.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent the prince Guchuo tegin, Chancellor Dide, and others at the head of three thousand horsemen to help suppress the rebels, and the emperor ordered Pugu Huai'en to take overall command.

sentences.zh: 又遣大首領蓋將軍與三女子謝婚，並告破堅昆功。

translations.literal: He also sent the great chieftain General Gai with three women to thank the marriage, and to report the merit of defeating Jian Kun.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the great chieftain General Gai with three women to thank the court for the marriage alliance and to report the victory over Jian Kun.

sentences.zh: 明年，骨啜與九節度戰相州，王師潰，帝德等奔京師，帝厚賜尉其意，乃還。

translations.literal: The next year Guchuo fought the nine military commissioners at Xiang Prefecture; the imperial army was routed; Dide and others fled to the capital; the emperor richly rewarded them to console their hearts, and they then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Guchuo fought the nine military commissioners at Xiang Prefecture. The imperial army was routed. Dide and the others fled to the capital. The emperor gave them rich rewards to console them, and they then returned home.

sentences.zh: 俄而可汗死，國人欲以公主殉，主曰：「中國人婿死，朝夕臨，喪期三年，此終禮也。

translations.literal: Before long the qaghan died. The people of the state wished the princess to follow in death. The princess said: "When a Chinese woman's husband dies, she attends morning and evening; the mourning period is three years—this is the full rite.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the qaghan died. His people wanted the princess to follow him in death. She said, "When a Chinese woman's husband dies, she attends him morning and evening, and mourning lasts three years—that is the full rite.

sentences.zh: 回紇萬里結昏，本慕中國，吾不可以殉。」

translations.literal: The Huihe came ten thousand li to marry, originally admiring China; I cannot follow in death.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe came ten thousand li to wed because they admired China. I cannot die with him.

sentences.zh: 乃止，然剺面哭，亦從其俗云。

translations.literal: They then ceased, yet she lacerated her face and wept, also following their custom.
translations.idiomatic: They relented, but she lacerated her face in mourning all the same, following their custom.

sentences.zh: 後以無子，得還。

translations.literal: Later, because she had no son, she was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because she had borne no son, she was allowed to return to China.

sentences.zh: 始葉護太子前得罪死，故次子移地健立，號牟羽可汗，其妻，仆固懷恩女也。

translations.literal: Earlier Crown Prince Yabghu had died after incurring guilt, so the second son Yidi Jian was enthroned, styled Qaghan Mouyu. His wife was a daughter of Pugu Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yabghu had earlier died after falling from favor, so the second son Yidi Jian succeeded him as Qaghan Mouyu. His wife was Pugu Huai'en's daughter.

sentences.zh: 始可汗為少子請昏，帝以妻之，至是為可敦。

translations.literal: The former qaghan had asked a marriage for his younger son; the emperor had given her to him; by now she was khatun.
translations.idiomatic: The late qaghan had asked the emperor to marry his younger son; the emperor had given him a bride, and she now became khatun.

sentences.zh: 明年，使大臣俱錄莫賀達干等入朝，並問公主起居，使人通謁於延英殿。

translations.literal: The next year he sent the high minister Julu Moyancho and others to court, also inquiring after the princess's health, with envoys granted audience in the Yanying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he sent the senior minister Julu Moyancho and others to court, inquiring after the princess's welfare as well. Their envoys were received in audience at the Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，以史朝義未滅，復遣中人劉清潭往結好，且發其兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, because Shi Chaoyi had not yet been destroyed, he again sent the palace man Liu Qingtan to renew friendship and also to mobilize their troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Shi Chaoyi was still at large, so he again sent the palace attendant Liu Qingtan to renew the alliance and summon Huihe troops.

sentences.zh: 比使者至，回紇已為朝義所訹，曰：「唐薦有喪，國無主，且亂，請回紇入收府庫，其富不貲。」

translations.literal: By the time the envoy arrived, the Huihe had already been seduced by Chaoyi, who said: "Tang has recently had a bereavement, the state has no ruler, and it is in disorder. Let the Huihe enter and seize the treasuries—the wealth is beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy arrived, Chaoyi had already swayed the Huihe with the claim that Tang had just lost its emperor, had no ruler, and was in chaos. "Let the Huihe march in and seize the treasuries," he said. "The wealth is beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 可汗即引兵南，八月也。

translations.literal: The qaghan thereupon led his army south—it was the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan thereupon led his army south. It was the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 清潭賫詔至其帳，可汗曰：「人言唐已亡，安得有使邪？」

translations.literal: Qingtan, bearing the patent, reached his camp. The qaghan said: "People say Tang is already destroyed—how can there be envoys?
translations.idiomatic: Qingtan arrived at the qaghan's camp with the imperial patent. The qaghan said, "People say Tang is already gone. How can there still be envoys?

sentences.zh: 清潭為言：「先帝雖棄天下，廣平王已即天子位，其仁聖英武類先帝，故與葉護收二京、破安慶緒者，是與可汗素厚，且唐歲給回紇繒絹，豈忘之邪？」

translations.literal: Qingtan spoke for him: "Though the late emperor has left the world, the Prince of Guangling has already taken the Son of Heaven's seat. He is benevolent, sagacious, heroic, and martial like the late emperor—you who with Yabghu recovered the two capitals and broke An Qingxu are old friends with the qaghan—and moreover Tang yearly gives the Huihe silks and gauzes. How could he forget that?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingtan replied, "The late emperor has indeed passed away, but the Prince of Guangling has already taken the throne. He is benevolent, wise, and martial like his father—the same ally who with Yabghu recovered the two capitals and destroyed An Qingxu, and whom you have long known. Besides, Tang pays the Huihe silks and gauzes every year. Would he forget that?"

sentences.zh: 是時，回紇已逾三城，見州縣榛萊，烽障無守，有輕唐色。

translations.literal: At that time the Huihe had already crossed the three passes. Seeing prefectures and counties overgrown with weeds and beacon towers undefended, they looked lightly on Tang.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Huihe had already crossed the frontier passes. Seeing prefectures and counties overgrown and undefended, they began to despise Tang.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使北收單于府兵、倉庫，數以語淩靳清潭。

translations.literal: He sent envoys north to gather the troops and granaries of the Chanyu Protectorate, repeatedly speaking thus to humiliate and rebuke Qingtan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys north to seize the troops and stores of the Chanyu Protectorate, repeatedly saying such things to humiliate Qingtan.

sentences.zh: 清潭密白帝：「回紇兵十萬向塞。」

translations.literal: Qingtan secretly reported to the emperor: "Huihe troops numbering one hundred thousand are advancing on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtan secretly reported to the emperor, "A hundred thousand Huihe soldiers are marching on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 朝廷震驚，遣殿中監藥子昂迎勞，且視軍，遇於太原，密識其兵裁四千，孺弱萬餘，馬四萬，與可敦偕來。

translations.literal: The court was alarmed and sent Yao Zi'ang of the Palace Directorate to welcome and comfort them and also to observe the army. They met at Taiyuan. He secretly reckoned their soldiers at only four thousand, with more than ten thousand women and children and forty thousand horses; the khatun had come with them.
translations.idiomatic: The court was alarmed and sent Yao Zi'ang of the Palace Directorate to welcome them, offer gifts, and inspect their forces. They met at Taiyuan. He secretly counted only four thousand fighting men, more than ten thousand women and children, and forty thousand horses. The khatun had come with them.

sentences.zh: 帝令懷恩與回紇會。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Huai'en to join with the Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Huai'en to link up with the Huihe.

sentences.zh: 因遣使上書，請助天子討賊。

translations.literal: They then sent envoys with a memorial asking to help the Son of Heaven suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe then sent envoys with a memorial offering to help the Son of Heaven suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 回紇欲入蒲關，徑沙苑而東，子昂說曰：「自寇亂來，州縣殘虛，供億無所資，且賊在東京，若入井陘，以取邢、洺、衛、懷，收賊財帑，乃鼓而南，上策也。」

translations.literal: The Huihe wished to enter Puguan Pass and go east straight through Shayuan. Zi'ang urged: "Since the rebellion, prefectures and counties lie ruined and empty, with nowhere to draw supplies. Moreover the rebels are in the Eastern Capital. If you enter Jingxing Pass to take Xing, Ming, Wei, and Huai, seize the rebels' wealth and stores, and then beat the drums south—that is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe wanted to enter through Puguan Pass and strike east across Shayuan. Zi'ang urged them, "Since the rebellion the countryside has been ruined and there is nothing to supply you. The rebels hold the Eastern Capital. If you take the Jingxing route to seize Xing, Ming, Wei, and Huai, gather their wealth and stores, and then march south beating the drums—that is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: They would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They refused.

sentences.zh: 子昂曰：「然則趨懷太行道，南據河陽，扼賊喉衿。」

translations.literal: Zi'ang said: "Then hasten along the Taihang route through Huai, seize Heyang to the south, and choke the rebels' throat.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang said, "Then take the Taihang road through Huai, hold Heyang to the south, and choke the rebels' lifeline.

sentences.zh: 又不聽。

translations.literal: Again they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Again they refused.

sentences.zh: 曰：「食太原倉粟，右次陜，與澤潞、河南、懷鄭兵合。」

translations.literal: He said: "Eat the grain of Taiyuan's granaries, then move right to Shan, and join the armies of Ze-Lu, Henan, and Huai-Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Eat grain from Taiyuan's granaries, then swing west to Shan and join the armies of Ze-Lu, Henan, and Huai-Zheng.

sentences.zh: 回紇從之。

translations.literal: The Huihe followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe accepted this plan.

sentences.zh: 詔以雍王為天下兵馬元帥，進子昂兼御史中丞，與右羽林衛將軍魏琚為左右廂兵馬使，中書舍人韋少華為元帥判官，御史中丞李進為行軍司馬，東會回紇。

translations.literal: An edict made the Prince of Yong commander-in-chief of all armies under heaven, promoted Zi'ang to concurrent censor-in-chief, made him and Right Wing Linwei General Wei Ju left and right wing army commanders, made Zhongshu Sheren Wei Shaohua the marshal's administrative aide and censor-in-chief Li Jin army march secretary, and ordered them east to join the Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed the Prince of Yong commander-in-chief of all armies under heaven, promoted Zi'ang to concurrent censor-in-chief, and paired him with Right Wing Linwei General Wei Ju as left and right wing commanders. Zhongshu Sheren Wei Shaohua became the marshal's chief aide, and Censor-in-Chief Li Jin became army march secretary. They marched east to join the Huihe.

sentences.zh: 敕元帥為諸軍先鋒，與諸節度會陜州。

translations.literal: The marshal was ordered to be vanguard of all armies and to join the military commissioners at Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was ordered to lead the vanguard of all armies and rendezvous with the military commissioners at Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時可汗壁陜州北，王往見之，可汗責王不蹈舞。

translations.literal: At that time the qaghan was encamped north of Shan Prefecture. The prince went to see him. The qaghan reproached the prince for not performing the treading dance.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan was then encamped north of Shan Prefecture. When the prince went to see him, the qaghan rebuked him for failing to perform the treading dance.

sentences.zh: 子昂辭曰：「王，嫡皇孫，二宮在殯，禮不可以蹈舞。」

translations.literal: Zi'ang declined, saying: "The prince is the legitimate imperial grandson. The two palaces are still in mourning—by ritual he cannot perform the treading dance.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang objected, "The prince is the legitimate imperial grandson. With the two palaces still in mourning, ritual forbids him to dance.

sentences.zh: 回紇廷詰曰：「可汗為唐天子弟，於王，叔父行也，容有不蹈舞乎？」

translations.literal: The Huihe pressed him in court, saying: "The qaghan is younger brother to the Son of Heaven of Tang—in relation to the prince he is an uncle. How can there be one who does not tread the dance?"
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe pressed him in open court. "The qaghan is the Tang emperor's younger brother," they said. "To the prince he is an uncle. How can he refuse to dance?"

sentences.zh: 子昂固拒，即言：「元帥，唐太子也，將君中國，而可舞蹈見可汗哉？」

translations.literal: Zi'ang firmly refused and said: "The marshal is Tang's crown prince, who will rule China—how can he dance before the qaghan?"
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang held firm. "The marshal is Tang's crown prince and future ruler of China. How can he dance before the qaghan?"

sentences.zh: 回紇君臣度不能屈，即引子昂、進、少華、琚搒之百，少華、琚一夕死，王還營。

translations.literal: The Huihe ruler and ministers saw they could not break him. They thereupon had Zi'ang, Jin, Shaohua, and Ju beaten a hundred strokes. Shaohua and Ju died within the night. The prince returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing they could not bend him, the Huihe ruler and his ministers had Zi'ang, Jin, Shaohua, and Ju flogged a hundred times. Shaohua and Ju died that night. The prince returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 官軍以王見辱，將合誅回紇，王以賊未滅止之。

translations.literal: The government armies, because the prince had been insulted, were about to unite in executing the Huihe. The prince stopped them because the rebels had not yet been destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies, furious at the insult to the prince, were ready to turn on the Huihe and destroy them, but the prince forbade it while the rebels still lived.

sentences.zh: 於是，懷恩與虜左殺為先驅。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huai'en and the barbarians' Zuo Sha served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en and the Huihe commander Zuo Sha then led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 朝義使反間，左殺執以獻，與諸將同擊賊，戰橫水，走之，進收東都。

translations.literal: Chaoyi sent agents to sow discord. Zuo Sha seized them and presented them. Together with the other generals they attacked the rebels, fought at Hengshui, drove them off, and advanced to recover the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi tried to sow discord through agents, but Zuo Sha seized them and handed them over. He and the other generals attacked the rebels, fought at Hengshui, routed them, and advanced to recover the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 可汗使拔賀那賀天子，獻朝義旗物。

translations.literal: The qaghan sent Bahana to congratulate the Son of Heaven and present Chaoyi's banners and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan sent Bahana to congratulate the emperor and present Chaoyi's banners and gear.

sentences.zh: 雍王還靈寶，可汗屯河陽，留三月，屯旁人困於剽辱。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yong returned to Lingbao. The qaghan camped at Heyang and remained three months. People near the camps were worn down by plunder and outrage.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong withdrew to Lingbao. The qaghan camped at Heyang for three months, and the people around his camps suffered relentless plunder and abuse.

sentences.zh: 仆固玚率回紇兵與朝義挐戰，蹀血二千里，梟其首，河北悉平。

translations.literal: Pugu Chang led Huihe troops to grapple in battle with Chaoyi, trampling blood for two thousand li. They took his head, and Hebei was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Chang led Huihe troops in a running fight with Chaoyi, trampling blood across two thousand li. They took his head, and Hebei was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 懷恩道相州西山崞口還屯，可汗出澤、潞，與懷恩會，道太原去。

translations.literal: Huai'en returned to encamp by way of Gukou in the western mountains of Xiang Prefecture. The qaghan exited through Ze and Lu, met with Huai'en, and departed by way of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en withdrew to camp by way of Gukou in the western hills of Xiang Prefecture. The qaghan marched out through Ze and Lu, met Huai'en, and left by way of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，回紇至東京，放兵攘剽，人皆遁保聖善、白馬二祠浮屠避之，回紇怒，火浮屠，殺萬餘人，及是益橫，詬折官吏，至以兵夜斫含光門，入鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Huihe reached the Eastern Capital they loosed their troops to plunder. People all fled to take refuge in the Buddhist pagodas of the Shengshan and Baima temples. The Huihe were enraged, fired the pagodas, and killed more than ten thousand people. By now they grew still more arrogant, reviling and humiliating officials, even sending troops by night to hack through the Hanguang Gate and enter the Honglu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huihe first reached the Eastern Capital they had let their soldiers plunder at will. People fled into the pagodas of the Shengshan and Baima monasteries for refuge. Enraged, the Huihe burned the pagodas and killed more than ten thousand people. Now they grew still bolder, insulting and browbeating officials, even sending troops by night to break through the Hanguang Gate and storm the Honglu Temple.

sentences.zh: 方其時，陜州節度使郭英乂留守東都，與魚朝恩及朔方軍驕肆，因回紇為暴，亦掠汝、鄭間，鄉不完廬，皆蔽紙為裳，虐於賊矣。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Yingyi, military commissioner of Shanzhou, was left to garrison the Eastern Capital. He, Yu Chao'en, and the Shuofang army were arrogant and overbearing. Relying on the Huihe's violence, they also plundered between Ru and Zheng. In the countryside no house stood whole; all covered themselves with paper for clothing—more cruel than the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guo Yingyi, military commissioner of Shanzhou, held the Eastern Capital as garrison commander. He, Yu Chao'en, and the Shuofang troops were arrogant and violent. Riding on the Huihe's depredations, they plundered between Ru and Zheng as well. In the countryside scarcely a whole house remained; people wrapped themselves in paper for clothing and suffered worse than under the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝念少華等死，故贈少華左散騎常侍，琚揚州大都督，賜一子六品官。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that Shaohua and the others had died, posthumously made Shaohua Left Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Ju Governor-General of Yang Prefecture, and granted one son a sixth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Shaohua's death and the others', the emperor posthumously appointed Shaohua Left Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Ju Governor-General of Yang Prefecture, and granted one son a sixth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 於是冊可汗曰頡咄登里骨啜蜜施合俱錄英義建功毗伽可汗，可敦曰娑墨光親麗華毗伽可敦，以左散騎常侍王翊使，即其牙命之，自可汗至宰相共賜實封二萬戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he invested the qaghan as Qaghan Keduo Dengli Guchuo Mishehe Julu Yingyi Jian Gong Pijia, and the khatun as Khatun Suomo Guangqin Lihua Pijia, with Wang Yi, Left Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, as envoy to invest him at the royal camp. From the qaghan down to the chancellors, all were granted twenty thousand households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: He then invested the qaghan as Keduo Dengli Guchuo Mishehe Julu Yingyi Jian Gong Pijia Qaghan and his consort as Suomo Guangqin Lihua Pijia Khatun, sending Wang Yi, Left Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, to invest them at the royal camp. From the qaghan down to his chancellors, each received a substantive fief of twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又以左殺為雄朔王，右殺寧朔王，胡祿都督金河王，拔鑒將軍靜漠王，十都督皆國公。

translations.literal: He also made Zuo Sha Prince of Xiongshuo, You Sha Prince of Ningshuo, the Hulu Protector Prince of Jinhe, General Bajian Prince of Jingmo, and the ten protectors all dukes of state.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed Zuo Sha as Prince of Xiongshuo, You Sha as Prince of Ningshuo, the Hulu Protector as Prince of Jinhe, General Bajian as Prince of Jingmo, and all ten tribal protectors as dukes of state.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，懷恩反，誘回紇、吐蕃入寇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongtai era Huai'en rebelled, tempting the Huihe and Tibetans to invade.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongtai era Huai'en rebelled and induced the Huihe and Tibetans to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 俄而懷恩死，二虜爭長，回紇首領潛詣涇陽見郭子儀，請改事。

translations.literal: Before long Huai'en died. The two barbarians contended for precedence. A Huihe chieftain secretly went to Jingyang to see Guo Ziyi and asked to change allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huai'en died. The two allies quarreled over precedence. A Huihe chieftain slipped away to Jingyang to see Guo Ziyi and offered to switch sides.

sentences.zh: 子儀率麾下叩回紇營。

translations.literal: Ziyi led his followers to knock at the Huihe camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi went with his escort to the Huihe camp.

sentences.zh: 回紇曰：「願見令公。」

translations.literal: The Huihe said: "We wish to see Lord Duke.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe said, "We wish to see Lord Duke.

sentences.zh: 子儀出旗門，回紇曰：「請釋甲。」

translations.literal: Ziyi went out the banner gate. The Huihe said: "Please lay aside your armor."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi stepped out through the banner gate. The Huihe said, "Lay aside your armor."

sentences.zh: 子儀易服。

translations.literal: Ziyi changed his dress.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi put off his armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 酋長相顧曰：「真是公矣！」

translations.literal: The chieftains looked at one another and said: "It truly is the lord!
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains looked at one another and exclaimed, "It truly is the lord!

sentences.zh: 時李光進、路嗣恭介馬在側，子儀示酋長曰：「此渭北節度使某，朔方軍糧使某。」

translations.literal: At that time Li Guangjin and Lu Sigong were at his side on horseback. Ziyi showed the chieftains and said: "This is a certain one, military commissioner of Weibei; this is a certain one, grain commissioner of Shuofang."
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangjin and Lu Sigong were then at his side on horseback. Ziyi pointed them out to the chieftains and said, "This is the military commissioner of Weibei; this is the grain commissioner of Shuofang."

sentences.zh: 酋長下馬拜，子儀亦下見之。

translations.literal: The chieftains dismounted and bowed; Ziyi also dismounted to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains dismounted and bowed. Ziyi dismounted to receive them in turn.

sentences.zh: 虜數百環視，子儀麾下亦至，子儀麾左右使卻，且命酒與飲，遺以纏頭彩三千，召可汗弟合胡祿等持手，因讓曰：「上念回紇功，報爾固厚，何負而來？

translations.literal: Several hundred barbarians ringed them in watching. Ziyi's followers also arrived. Ziyi waved his attendants to withdraw, ordered wine for them to drink, gave three thousand bolts of headcloth silks, called the qaghan's younger brother He Hulu and others to take his hand, and reproached them, saying: "The emperor, mindful of Huihe merit, has repaid you thickly—why have you failed us and come?
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of tribesmen ringed them round. Ziyi's own men arrived as well. He waved his attendants back, ordered wine, and gave three thousand bolts of headcloth silks. Taking the qaghan's younger brother He Hulu and others by the hand, he reproached them: "The emperor remembers your service to Tang and has rewarded you richly. Why have you betrayed us and come?

sentences.zh: 今即與汝戰，何遽降也？

translations.literal: If I fight you now, why have you hurried to submit?
translations.idiomatic: If I fight you now, why have you come begging peace so quickly?

sentences.zh: 我將獨入爾營，雖殺我，吾將士能擊汝。」

translations.literal: I will enter your camp alone; even if you kill me, my officers and men can strike you down.
translations.idiomatic: I will enter your camp alone. Even if you kill me, my soldiers can still destroy you.

sentences.zh: 酋長詟服曰：「懷恩詭我曰『唐天子南走，公見廢』，是以來。

translations.literal: The chieftains submitted in awe and said: "Huai'en deceived us, saying 'The Son of Heaven has fled south and the lord has been dismissed'—that is why we came.
translations.idiomatic: Awed, the chieftains submitted. "Huai'en tricked us," they said. "He told us the Son of Heaven had fled south and that you had been removed. That is why we came.

sentences.zh: 今天可汗在，公無恙，吾等願還擊吐蕃以報厚恩。

translations.literal: Today the qaghan is alive, the lord is unharmed, and we wish to turn back and strike the Tibetans to repay your thick kindness.
translations.idiomatic: But the qaghan lives, you are safe, and we are willing to turn back and attack the Tibetans to repay your kindness.

sentences.zh: 然懷恩子，可敦弟也，願赦死。」

translations.literal: Yet Huai'en's son is the khatun's younger brother—we beg his life be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's son, however, is the khatun's brother. We beg you to spare his life."

sentences.zh: 於是子儀持酒，胡祿請盟而飲，子儀曰：「唐天子萬歲，回紇可汗亦萬歲，二國將相如之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ziyi held the wine. He Hulu asked to swear alliance and drink. Ziyi said: "Long live the Son of Heaven of Tang; long live the Huihe qaghan; may the two states' generals and chancellors be as this.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi raised the wine. He Hulu asked to swear and drink together. Ziyi said, "Long live the Son of Heaven of Tang! Long live the Huihe qaghan! May the ministers and generals of both states be as we are now.

sentences.zh: 有如負約，身死行陣，家屠戮。」

translations.literal: If anyone breaks the pact, may he die in battle and his house be slaughtered."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone breaks this oath, may he die on the field and his house be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 方時，虜宰相磨咄莫賀達干、頓莫賀達干等聞言皆奪氣，酒至其所，輒曰：「無易公誓。」

translations.literal: At that time the barbarian chancellors Modu Moyancho, Dun Moyancho, and others, hearing this, all lost their spirit. When the wine reached them they would say: "Do not change the lord's oath."
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe chancellors Modu Moyancho, Dun Moyancho, and others lost heart at his words. When the cup reached them they would say only, "Do not change the lord's oath."

sentences.zh: 始，虜有二巫，言「此行必不戰，當見大人而還」；

translations.literal: Earlier the barbarians had had two shamans who said: "On this campaign there will surely be no battle; we shall see a great man and return";
translations.idiomatic: Earlier two Huihe shamans had declared, "This campaign will bring no battle. We shall see a great man and return."

sentences.zh: 及是相顧笑曰：「巫不吾紿也。」

translations.literal: and now they looked at one another and laughed, saying: "The shamans did not deceive us."
translations.idiomatic: Now they looked at one another and laughed. "The shamans did not lie to us," they said.

translations.literal: So they ended.
translations.idiomatic: So they ended.

sentences.zh: 朔方先鋒兵馬使白元光合回紇兵於靈臺，會雪嚴晦，吐蕃閉營撤備，乃縱擊之，斬首五萬級，生禽萬人，獲馬、橐它、牛、羊，收所俘唐戶五千。

translations.literal: Shuofang vanguard army commander Bai Yuanguang joined Huihe troops at Lingtai. It happened that snow fell thick and dark; the Tibetans closed camp and relaxed their guard. He then loosed an attack, beheading fifty thousand, capturing ten thousand alive, taking horses, camels, cattle, and sheep, and recovering five thousand Tang households who had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yuanguang, Shuofang's vanguard commander, joined Huihe forces at Lingtai. Snow fell thick and the sky was dark. The Tibetans shut their camps and dropped their guard. He then struck, beheading fifty thousand men, taking ten thousand alive, and seizing horses, camels, cattle, and sheep. He also recovered five thousand Tang subjects who had been captured.

sentences.zh: 仆固名臣降，合胡祿都督等二百人皆來朝，賜與不可計。

translations.literal: Pugu Mingchen surrendered; He Hulu the protector and two hundred others all came to court, and gifts beyond reckoning were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Mingchen surrendered. He Hulu the protector and two hundred others came to court, and rewards beyond counting were lavished on them.

sentences.zh: 子儀以名臣見。

translations.literal: Ziyi presented Mingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi presented Mingchen to the throne.

sentences.zh: 名臣，懷恩兄子，銳將也。

translations.literal: Mingchen was Huai'en's elder brother's son—a sharp commander.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen was Huai'en's nephew, a fierce commander.

sentences.zh: ，光親可敦卒，帝遣右散騎常侍蕭昕持節吊祠。

translations.literal: Khatun Guangqin died. The emperor sent Xiao Xin, Right Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, bearing credentials to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Khatun Guangqin died. The emperor sent Xiao Xin, Right Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, with credentials to offer condolences and perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 明年，以懷恩幼女為崇徽公主繼室，兵部侍郎李涵持節冊拜可敦，賜繒彩二萬。

translations.literal: The next year he gave Huai'en's young daughter in marriage as Princess Chonghui to succeed her, and sent Li Han, Vice Minister of War, with credentials to invest her as khatun, granting twenty thousand bolts of silks.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he married Huai'en's young daughter to the qaghan as Princess Chonghui, succeeding the late khatun. Li Han, Vice Minister of War, was sent with credentials to invest her, and twenty thousand bolts of silks were granted.

sentences.zh: 是時，財用屈，稅公卿騾、橐它給行，宰相餞中渭橋。

translations.literal: At that time finances were strained; they levied mules and camels from the nobles to supply the mission, and the chief ministers saw them off at the Zhongwei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Finances were strained at the time. The court levied mules and camels from high officials to equip the mission, and the chief ministers saw them off at the Zhongwei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 回紇之留京師者，曹輩掠女子於市，引騎犯含光門，皇城皆闔，詔劉清潭慰止。

translations.literal: Those Huihe who remained in the capital—petty fellows—snatched women in the markets and led horsemen to break through the Hanguang Gate. The entire imperial city was shut. An edict sent Liu Qingtan to comfort and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Huihe who remained in the capital were robbing women in the markets and riding through the Hanguang Gate. The whole imperial city was shut tight. The emperor sent Liu Qingtan to calm them.

sentences.zh: 復出暴市物，奪長安令邵說馬，有司不敢何詰。

translations.literal: They again went out to plunder goods in the markets and seized the horse of the mayor of Chang'an, Shao Yue. The authorities did not dare question them.
translations.idiomatic: They went out again to loot the markets and seized the horse of Shao Yue, mayor of Chang'an. The authorities did not dare intervene.

sentences.zh: 自乾元後，益負功，每納一馬，取直四十縑，歲以數萬求售，使者相躡，留舍鴻臚，駘弱不可用，帝厚賜欲以愧之，不知也。

translations.literal: From the Qianyuan era onward they grew still more arrogant over their merit. For each horse presented they took payment of forty bolts of silk; every year they sought to sell tens of thousands. Envoys came in unbroken succession and lodged at the Honglu Temple with worn, weak horses unusable for service. The emperor richly rewarded them hoping to shame them—they did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianyuan era they grew bolder still on account of their service. For every horse they presented they demanded forty bolts of silk, and each year they offered tens of thousands for sale. Envoys arrived in endless succession and lodged at the Honglu Temple with worn, useless nags. The emperor heaped gifts on them hoping to shame them into moderation, but they never understood.

sentences.zh: 復以萬馬來，帝不忍重煩民，為償六千。

translations.literal: They again brought ten thousand horses. The emperor could not bear to burden the people further and paid for six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They brought ten thousand horses again. Unwilling to burden the people further, the emperor bought six thousand.

sentences.zh: 十年，回紇殺人橫道，京兆尹黎幹捕之，詔貸勿劾。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Huihe killed people in the open road. Jingzhao Yin Li Gan arrested them. An edict pardoned them and forbade prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Huihe killed people in the streets. Li Gan, intendant of Jingzhao, arrested the culprits. An edict ordered their release and forbade prosecution.

sentences.zh: 又刺人東市，縛送萬年獄，首領劫取囚，殘獄吏去，都人厭苦。

translations.literal: They again stabbed a man in the eastern market, bound him, and sent him to the Wan'ian jail. A chieftain seized the prisoner, mutilated the jail officers, and left. The people of the capital were sick of it.
translations.idiomatic: They stabbed another man in the eastern market, bound him, and sent him to the Wan'ian jail. A chieftain seized the prisoner, maimed the jailers, and rode off. The people of the capital were worn past endurance.

sentences.zh: 十三年，回紇襲振武，攻東陘，入寇太原。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Huihe raided Zhenwu, attacked Dongxing, and invaded Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Huihe raided Zhenwu, attacked Dongxing, and invaded Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使鮑防與戰陽曲，防敗績，殘殺萬人。

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Bao Fang fought them at Yangqu. Fang was badly defeated and more than ten thousand were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Fang, military commissioner of Hedong, met them at Yangqu and was routed. More than ten thousand people were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 代州都督張光晟又戰羊虎谷，破之，虜乃去。

translations.literal: Daizhou Protector Zhang Guangcheng again fought them at Yanghugu and broke them; the barbarians then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangcheng, protector of Daizhou, fought them again at Yanghugu and defeated them, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，使中人告喪，且脩好。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne he sent a palace man to announce the bereavement and also to renew friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne he sent a palace attendant to announce the late emperor's death and renew the alliance.

sentences.zh: 時九姓胡勸可汗入寇，可汗欲悉師向塞，見使者不為禮。

translations.literal: At that time the Nine Surnames Hu urged the qaghan to invade. The qaghan wished to lead his entire army on the frontier. Seeing the envoy he showed no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Surnames Hu were then urging the qaghan to raid. He meant to march his whole army on the frontier and treated the envoy with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 宰相頓莫賀達干曰：「唐，大國，無負於我。

translations.literal: Chancellor Dun Moyancho said: "Tang is a great state and has not failed us.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dun Moyancho said, "Tang is a great power and has done us no wrong.

sentences.zh: 前日入太原，取羊馬數萬，比及國，亡耗略盡。

translations.literal: The other day we entered Taiyuan and took tens of thousands of sheep and horses; by the time we reached home, nearly all were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When we raided Taiyuan we took tens of thousands of sheep and horses, yet by the time we reached home almost all were gone.

sentences.zh: 今舉國遠鬥，有如不捷，將安歸？」

translations.literal: Now if the whole nation fights far away and we do not prevail, where shall we return?
translations.idiomatic: If we march the whole nation far to fight and do not win, where will we go home to?

sentences.zh: 可汗不聽，頓莫賀怒，因擊殺之，並屠其支黨及九姓胡幾二千人，即自立為合骨咄祿毗伽可汗，使長建達干從使者入朝。

translations.literal: The qaghan would not listen. Dun Moyancho was enraged, struck and killed him, and also slaughtered his branch kin and the Nine Surnames Hu—nearly two thousand in all. He thereupon enthroned himself as Qaghan He'gulu Pijia, and sent Chief Minister Chang Jiandagan to follow the envoy to court.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan refused to listen. Enraged, Dun Moyancho struck him down and slaughtered his kin and the Nine Surnames Hu as well—nearly two thousand people in all. He then proclaimed himself Qaghan He'gulu Pijia and sent Chief Minister Chang Jiandagan to court with the envoy.

sentences.zh: ，詔京兆少尹源休持節冊頓莫賀為武義成功可汗。

translations.literal: An edict sent Yuan Xiu, Vice Director of the Capital, with credentials to invest Dun Moyancho as Qaghan Wuyi Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuan Xiu, Vice Director of the Capital, with credentials to invest Dun Moyancho as Qaghan Wuyi Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 始回紇至中國，常參以九姓胡，往往留京師，至千人，居貲殖產甚厚。

translations.literal: From the time the Huihe first came to China they regularly brought the Nine Surnames Hu with them. Many often remained in the capital—at times as many as a thousand—amassing wealth and property in great abundance.
