translations.literal: The Black Cart tribe, glad at their weakness, thereupon killed Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: The Black Cart tribe, glad at their weakness, thereupon killed Wujie.

sentences.zh: 其下又奉其弟遏撚特勒為可汗。

translations.literal: His followers again enthroned his younger brother Tegin Enian as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: His followers again enthroned his younger brother Tegin Enian as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 帝詔德裕紀功銘石於幽州，以誇後世。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Deyu to inscribe a stele recording achievements at Youzhou, to glorify posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Deyu to inscribe a victory stele at Youzhou, that later ages might read of the triumph.

sentences.zh: 思忠等以國亡，皆願入朝，見聽，遂罷歸義軍，擢思忠左監門衛上將軍兼撫王傅，兩稟其奉，賜第永樂坊，分其兵賜諸節度。

translations.literal: Sizhong and the others, because their state had perished, all wished to enter court. Permission was granted. The Guyi Army was abolished. Sizhong was promoted to Left Superior General of the Jianmen Guards and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Fu, receiving stipends from both offices. A residence in Yongle Ward was granted, and their troops were distributed among the various circuit commands.
translations.idiomatic: Because their state was gone, Sizhong and his fellows all asked to come to court, and the request was granted. The Guyi Army was dissolved. Sizhong was made Left Superior General of the Jianmen Guards and tutor to the Prince of Fu, drawing pay from both posts. He was given a mansion in Yongle Ward, and their soldiers were parceled out to the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 虜人憚隸食諸道，據滹沱河叛，劉沔坑殺三千人。

translations.literal: The barbarians feared being assigned as subordinates to feed the various circuits. They seized the Hutuo River and rebelled. Liu Mian buried alive three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen dreaded being parcelled out as dependents to feed the various circuits. They seized the Hutuo River and rose in revolt. Liu Mian had three thousand of them buried alive.

sentences.zh: 詔回鶻營功德使在二京者，悉冠帶之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Uyghur merit commissioners stationed in the two capitals should all wear official caps and belts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded that Uyghur merit commissioners serving in the two capitals should all be given official caps and sashes.

sentences.zh: 有司收摩尼書若象燒於道，產貲入之官。

translations.literal: The authorities collected Manichaean books and images, burned them in the streets, and confiscated property into the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Officials seized Manichaean scriptures and images, burned them in the roads, and turned confiscated goods over to the government.

sentences.zh: 遏撚可汗裒殘部五千，仰食於奚大酋碩舍朗。

translations.literal: Qaghan Enian gathered five thousand survivors and depended on the Xi grand chief Shuoshelang for food.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Enian mustered five thousand broken followers and lived at the mercy of the Xi grand chief Shuoshelang.

sentences.zh: 大中初，仲武討奚，破之，回鶻浸耗滅，所存名王貴臣五百餘，轉依室韋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era, Zhongwu campaigned against the Xi and defeated them. The Uyghurs gradually dwindled away. Only five hundred-odd titled kings and nobles remained, shifting to depend on the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong reign, Zhang Zhongwu attacked the Xi and broke them. The Uyghurs dwindled steadily; only some five hundred titled kings and nobles survived, drifting to take shelter with the Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 仲武諭令羈致可汗等，遏撚懼，挾妻葛祿、子特勒毒斯馳九騎夜委眾西走，部人皆慟哭。

translations.literal: Zhongwu ordered them to capture and bring in the qaghan and others. Enian was afraid. Taking his wife Gelu and his son Tegin Dusi, he rode nine horsemen by night, abandoned his followers, and fled west. His tribesmen all wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu instructed his men to seize the qaghan and his party. Enian was terrified. With his wife Gelu and his son Tegin Dusi he took nine riders and fled west by night, abandoning the host. The whole tribe wept.

sentences.zh: 室韋七姓析回鶻隸之。

translations.literal: The seven Shiwei clans divided the Uyghurs and made them subject.
translations.idiomatic: The seven Shiwei clans carved up the Uyghurs and took them as subjects.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯怒，與其相阿播將兵七萬擊室韋，悉收回鶻還磧北。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz were enraged. With their chancellor A Bo they led seventy thousand troops to attack the Shiwei and wholly recovered the Uyghurs, returning them north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz were furious. Their chancellor A Bo marched seventy thousand men against the Shiwei, recovered every Uyghur remnant, and brought them back north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 遺帳伏山林間，狙盜諸蕃自給，稍歸厖特勒。

translations.literal: Remnant camps hid in mountains and forests, ambushing and robbing various tribes to sustain themselves, and gradually returned to Tegin Pang.
translations.idiomatic: Stragglers hid in the hills, waylaying other tribes for a living, and little by little rallied again to Tegin Pang.

sentences.zh: 是時，特勒已自稱可汗，居甘州，有磧西諸城。

translations.literal: At this time the tegin had already styled himself qaghan, dwelt at Ganzhou, and held the various cities west of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: By then the tegin had already proclaimed himself qaghan, ruled from Ganzhou, and held the towns west of the desert.

sentences.zh: 宣宗務綏柔荒遠，遣使者抵靈州省其酋長，回鶻因遣人隨使者來京師，帝即冊拜嗢祿登裏邏汨沒蜜施合俱錄毗伽懷建可汗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong devoted himself to soothing the distant frontier regions. He sent envoys to Lingzhou to visit their chieftains. The Uyghurs therefore sent men following the envoys to the capital. The emperor thereupon invested and enfeoffed Wuluodengli Luomo Mimi Shihejulupiji Huaijian as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sought to win over the far frontiers. He sent envoys to Lingzhou to call on their chiefs. The Uyghurs sent men with the envoys to the capital, and the emperor at once invested Wuluodengli Luomo Mimi Shihejulupiji Huaijian as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，一再獻方物。

translations.literal: For more than ten years afterward they presented regional products once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: For the next dozen years they sent tribute goods once or twice.

sentences.zh: 懿宗時，大酋仆固俊自北庭擊吐蕃，斬論尚熱盡取西州、輪臺等城，使達幹米懷玉朝且獻俘，因請命，詔可。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yizong, the grand chief Pugu Jun from Beiting attacked the Tibetans, beheaded Lun Shangre, and took Xizhou, Luntai, and other cities. He sent taghan Mi Huaiyu to court with captives and requested appointment. An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Yizong, the great chief Pugu Jun marched from Beiting against Tibet, slew Lun Shangre, and seized Xizhou, Luntai, and the rest. He sent taghan Mi Huaiyu to court with prisoners and asked for a commission; the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 其後王室亂，貢會不常，史亡其傳。

translations.literal: Afterward the royal house fell into disorder. Tribute audiences were irregular, and the histories lose their record.
translations.idiomatic: After that the royal house fell into chaos, tribute came fitfully, and the histories lose the thread.

sentences.zh: 昭宗幸鳳翔，靈州節度使韓遜表回鶻請率兵赴難，翰林學士韓偓曰：「虜為國仇舊矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong went to Fengxiang. Lingzhou Military Commissioner Han Xun memorialized that the Uyghurs offered to lead troops to rescue the crisis. Han Wo said: "The barbarians have long been old enemies of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong took refuge at Fengxiang, Han Xun, military commissioner of Lingzhou, reported that the Uyghurs wished to march to the emperor's aid. Han Wo said, "These tribes have been the empire's ancient foe.

sentences.zh: 自會昌時伺邊，羽翼未成，不得逞。

translations.literal: Since Huichang they watched our borders; their wings were not yet full and they could not act.
translations.idiomatic: Since Huichang they have watched our borders. Their wings were not yet grown, and they could not strike.

sentences.zh: 今乘我危以冀幸，不可開也。」

translations.literal: Now they take advantage of our danger to hope for luck—this opening must not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Now they seize our peril to gamble on fortune. This door must not be opened.

sentences.zh: 遂格不報。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was blocked and no reply sent.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was set aside and no answer given.

sentences.zh: 然其國卒不振，時時以玉、馬與邊州相市雲。

translations.literal: Yet their state ultimately did not revive, and from time to time they bartered jade and horses with border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their kingdom never truly revived; they traded jade and horses with the border prefectures from time to time.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀者，先與薛種雜居，後滅延陀部有之，號薛延陀，姓一利咥氏。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo originally lived mixed with the Xue tribe; later, having destroyed the Yantuo tribe, they took the name Xueyantuo. Their surname was Yilishijia.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo had first lived intermingled with the Xue clan; after they destroyed the Yantuo tribe they took the compound name Xueyantuo. Their lineage was the Yilishijia clan.

sentences.zh: 在鐵勒諸部最雄張，風俗大抵與突厥同。

translations.literal: Among the Tiele tribes they were the most powerful; their customs were largely the same as the Turks'.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the Tiele tribes they were the strongest, and their ways differed little from the Turks'.

sentences.zh: 西突厥處羅可汗之殺鐵勒諸酋也，其下往往相率叛去，推契哥楞為易勿真莫賀可汗，據貪汗山，奉薛延陀乙失缽為野咥可汗，保燕末山。

translations.literal: When Western Turk qaghan Chuluo killed the Tiele chiefs, their followers often rebelled in succession. They enthroned Qigeling as Yiwuzhen Mohe qaghan, holding Mount Tanhan, and installed Yishibo's Yishibo as Yedie qaghan, guarding Mount Yanmo.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Turk qaghan Chuluo slew the Tiele chiefs, their people rose in one revolt after another. They set up Qigeling as Yiwuzhen Mohe qaghan on Mount Tanhan and made Yishibo's Yishibo Yedie qaghan, holding Mount Yanmo.

sentences.zh: 而突厥射匱可汗復強，二部黜可汗號往臣之。

translations.literal: Then the Turk qaghan Shekui grew strong again, and the two divisions deposed their qaghan titles and became his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turk qaghan Shekui regained power, both divisions set aside their qaghan titles and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 回紇、拔野古、阿跌、同羅、仆骨、白霫在郁督軍山者，東附始畢可汗；

translations.literal: The Huihe, Bayegu, Adie, Tongluo, Pugu, and Baixi at Mount Yudujun in the east attached themselves to Qaghan Shibi;
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe, Bayegu, Adie, Tongluo, Pugu, and Baixi at Mount Yudujun in the east submitted to Qaghan Shibi;

sentences.zh: 乙失缽在金山者，西役葉護可汗。

translations.literal: Yishibo at Mount Jinshan in the west served Qaghan Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: Yishibo at Mount Jinshan in the west served under Qaghan Yehu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，葉護死，其國亂，乙失缽孫曰夷男，率部帳七萬附頡利可汗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Yehu died and his state fell into disorder. Yishibo's grandson, called Yi Nan, led seventy thousand tents to attach themselves to Qaghan Jieli.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan, Yehu died and the realm fell into chaos. Yishibo's grandson Yi Nan led seventy thousand tents to submit to Qaghan Jieli.

sentences.zh: 後突厥衰，夷男反攻頡利，弱之，於是諸姓多叛頡利，歸之者共推為主，夷男不敢當。

translations.literal: Later the Turks declined. Yi Nan counterattacked Jieli and weakened him. Thereupon many clans rebelled against Jieli and, those who returned, jointly urged him as lord—but Yi Nan did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks weakened, Yi Nan turned on Jieli and wore him down. Many tribes then deserted Jieli; those who came over jointly urged Yi Nan to rule, but he dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 明年，太宗方圖頡利，遣遊擊將軍喬師望路賫詔書、鼓纛，冊拜夷男為真珠毗伽可汗。

translations.literal: The next year, as Taizong was plotting against Jieli, he sent Strike-General Qiao Shiwang by a roundabout route bearing edicts, drums, and banners, investing Yi Nan as Zhenzhu Pijia qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, while Taizong was moving against Jieli, he sent Strike-General Qiao Shiwang by a detour with edicts, drums, and banners to invest Yi Nan as Zhenzhu Pijia qaghan.

sentences.zh: 夷男已受命，遣使謝，歸方物，乃樹牙郁督軍山，直京師西北六千里，東靺鞨，西葉護突厥，南沙磧，北俱倫水，地大眾附，於是回紇等諸部莫不伏屬。

translations.literal: Yi Nan, having received the appointment, sent envoys to give thanks and return regional products. He then planted his royal camp at Mount Yudujun, six thousand li northwest of the capital—Mohe to the east, Yehu's Turks to the west, the southern desert to the south, and the Kherlen River to the north. The land was broad and the people numerous. Thereupon the Huihe and other tribes all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once invested, Yi Nan sent envoys with thanks and tribute. He pitched his royal camp at Mount Yudujun, six thousand li northwest of the capital: Mohe to the east, Yehu's Turks to the west, the southern desert to the south, the Kherlen to the north. His domain was vast and his following great, and the Huihe and the rest all bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 其弟統特勒入朝，帝以精刀、寶鞭賜之曰：「下有大過者，以吾鞭鞭之。」

translations.literal: His younger brother Tegin Tong entered court. The emperor gave him a fine blade and a precious whip, saying: "If any below commits a grave fault, beat him with my whip.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tegin Tong came to court. The emperor gave him a fine blade and a jeweled whip, saying, "If anyone beneath you commits a grave offense, strike him with my whip.

sentences.zh: 夷男以為寵。

translations.literal: Yi Nan took this as favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Nan regarded this as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗之滅，塞隧空荒，夷男率其部稍東，保都尉楗山獨邏水之陰，遠京師才三千里而贏，東室韋，西金山，南突厥，北瀚海，蓋古匈奴地也。

translations.literal: When Qaghan Jieli was destroyed, the frontier passes stood empty. Yi Nan led his tribe somewhat eastward, holding Mount Dujian alone on the north bank of the Tula River—only three thousand li from the capital and close. Shiwei lay to the east, Mount Jinshan to the west, the Turks to the south, and the Sea of Khara-Nur to the north. It was the old land of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's fall the frontier stood empty. Yi Nan shifted his people eastward to Mount Dujian on the north bank of the Tula, only three thousand li from the capital and near at hand: Shiwei east, Mount Jinshan west, Turks south, Khara-Nur north—the ancient Xiongnu domain.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二十萬，以二子大度設、突利失分將之，號南、北部。

translations.literal: His fighting men numbered two hundred thousand. He divided command between his two sons Dadu She and Tuli Shi, styled the southern and northern wings.
translations.idiomatic: He could field two hundred thousand warriors. His sons Dadu She and Tuli Shi each commanded a wing, called the southern and northern divisions.

sentences.zh: 七年間，使者八朝。

translations.literal: Within seven years envoys came to court eight times.
translations.idiomatic: Within seven years his envoys came to court eight times.

sentences.zh: 帝恐後強大為患，欲產其禍，乃下詔拜其二子皆為小可汗。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that later they would grow strong and become a trouble, and wished to sow discord among them. He issued an edict investing both sons as lesser qaghans.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared they would grow too mighty and become a threat, and wished to breed trouble among them. He issued an edict making both sons lesser qaghans.

sentences.zh: 十五年，帝以李思摩為可汗，始度河，牙於漠南。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor made Li Simo qaghan. He first crossed the river and planted his camp south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor set up Li Simo as qaghan. Simo crossed the river for the first time and pitched his camp south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 夷男惡之，未發。

translations.literal: Yi Nan hated this and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Nan resented this and held back.

sentences.zh: 方帝幸洛陽，將遂封泰山，夷男與其下謀曰：「天子封泰山，萬國皆助兵，悉會行在，邊鄣空單，思摩可取也。」

translations.literal: Just as the emperor was visiting Luoyang and about to perform the Feng and Shan rites on Mount Tai, Yi Nan plotted with his followers, saying: "When the Son of Heaven performs Feng and Shan, all states send troops to assist. They will all gather at the imperial camp, the frontier will stand empty, and Simo can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Luoyang preparing to ascend Mount Tai for the Feng and Shan sacrifices, Yi Nan said to his men, "When the Son of Heaven mounts Tai, every state sends troops. They will all crowd the imperial camp and leave the frontier bare—then Simo is ours.

sentences.zh: 乃使大度設勒兵二十萬，南絕漠，壁白道川，率一兵得四馬，擊思摩。

translations.literal: He then sent Dadu She to lead two hundred thousand troops south across the desert, encamping on the Baidao River, with one soldier taking four horses, to attack Simo.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Dadu She with two hundred thousand men south across the desert to camp on the Baidao River, four horses to every soldier, to strike Simo.

sentences.zh: 思摩走朔州，言狀，且請師。

translations.literal: Simo fled to Shuozhou, reported the situation, and asked for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Simo fled to Shuozhou, reported what had happened, and begged for aid.

sentences.zh: 於是詔營州都督張儉統所部與奚、霫、契丹乘其東，朔州道行軍總管李勣眾六萬、騎三千，營朔州，靈州道行軍總管李大亮眾四萬、騎五千，屯靈武，慶州道行軍總管張士貴眾萬七千出雲中，涼州道行軍總管李襲譽經略之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Yingzhou Protector-General Zhang Jian to lead his command together with the Xi, Xi, and Khitan to strike their east. Shuozhou Route Campaign Commander-in-Chief Li Ji had sixty thousand men and three thousand cavalry and encamped at Shuozhou. Lingzhou Route Commander-in-Chief Li Daliang had forty thousand men and five thousand cavalry and encamped at Lingwu. Qingzhou Route Commander-in-Chief Zhang Shigui had seventeen thousand and advanced from Yunzhong. Liangzhou Route Commander-in-Chief Li Xiyu directed overall strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts went out: Zhang Jian of Yingzhou was to hit their eastern flank with the Xi, Xi, and Khitan; Li Ji on the Shuozhou route camped with sixty thousand foot and three thousand horse; Li Daliang on the Lingzhou route held Lingwu with forty thousand foot and five thousand horse; Zhang Shigui on the Qingzhou route marched seventeen thousand from Yunzhong; Li Xiyu on the Liangzhou route coordinated the whole.

sentences.zh: 帝敕諸將曰：「延陀度漠，馬已疲。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the generals: "The Xueyantuo have crossed the desert and their horses are already weary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his generals, "The Xueyantuo have crossed the desert—their horses are spent.

sentences.zh: 夫用兵者，見利疾進，不利亟去。

translations.literal: In warfare, when you see profit advance swiftly; when it is not profitable withdraw quickly.
translations.idiomatic: In war, press hard when gain is clear; withdraw swiftly when it is not.

sentences.zh: 今虜不急擊思摩，又不速還，勢必敗，卿等勿與戰，須其歸，可擊也。」

translations.literal: Now the barbarians neither press Simo in haste nor return quickly—they are sure to be defeated. Do not engage them in battle; wait until they retreat, then you may strike.
translations.idiomatic: These tribes neither hurry to finish Simo nor turn back—they are bound to lose. Do not give battle; wait until they withdraw, then strike.

sentences.zh: 既而延陀使者來，求與突厥平。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xueyantuo envoys came seeking peace with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xueyantuo envoys arrived asking peace with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我約漠以北，延陀制之，漠以南，突厥專之，有輒相掠，誅不赦。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I decreed that north of the desert the Xueyantuo should rule, and south of the desert the Turks alone—whoever raided the other would be put to death without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I decreed that north of the desert the Xueyantuo should rule and south of the desert the Turks alone; any who raided across the line would die without mercy.

sentences.zh: 延陀父事我而首違詔，得非亂邪？

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo treat me as father yet first violate the edict—is this not rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo call me father yet break my edict first—is that not rebellion?

sentences.zh: 而曰與突厥和，乃故約也，尚何請？」

translations.literal: Yet you speak of peace with the Turks—that is the old pact. What more is there to ask?
translations.idiomatic: And now you speak of peace with the Turks—that was the old bargain. What more is there to plead for?

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was sent.
translations.idiomatic: No answer was given.

sentences.zh: 大度設次長城，思摩已南走，大度設度不可得，乃遣人乘長城罵之。

translations.literal: Dadu She encamped at the Great Wall. Simo had already fled south. Dadu She could not overtake him and sent men to ride the wall and revile him.
translations.idiomatic: Dadu She halted at the Great Wall. Simo was already gone south; Dadu She could not catch him and sent men along the wall to curse him.

sentences.zh: 適會勣兵至，行壒屬天，遽率眾走赤柯，度青山，然道回遠，勣選敢死士與突騎徑臘河，趣白道，及大度設，尾之不置。

translations.literal: Just then Li Ji's troops arrived. Dust from the marching columns filled the sky. He immediately led his force to Chike, crossed the Green Mountains by a roundabout route, and pursued along the Baidao. He caught Dadu She and pressed him without respite.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji's army came up; dust from the columns blotted the sky. He wheeled his host to Chike, swung through the Green Mountains by a long detour, crossed the frozen river, took the Baidao, caught Dadu She, and never let up the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 大度設顧不脫，度諾真水，陣以待。

translations.literal: Dadu She looked back and could not shake them off. He crossed the Nuozhen River and formed battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Dadu She glanced back and could not shake them. He crossed the Nuozhen River and drew up for battle.

sentences.zh: 先是，延陀擊沙缽羅及阿史那社爾，皆以徒戰勝，至是卻騎不用，率五人為伍，一執馬，四前鬥，令曰：「勝則騎而逐，負者死，沒其家以償戰士。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the Xueyantuo had attacked Shaboluo and Ashina She'er and in each case won with infantry. Now they dismounted and did not use their horses, forming groups of five—one holding the horses, four fighting ahead—with the order: "If you win, mount and pursue; if you lose, you die, and your household is forfeited to compensate the warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the Xueyantuo had beaten Shaboluo and Ashina She'er fighting on foot. Now they left their horses, formed fives—one man holding four horses while four fought on foot—and ordered, "Win, mount and chase; lose, die, and your family is forfeit to pay the warriors.

sentences.zh: 及戰，突厥兵迮，延陀騰逐，勣救之，延陀縱射，馬輒死。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, the Turk troops were pressed tight. The Xueyantuo leaped up and pursued. Li Ji came to the rescue. The Xueyantuo loosed arrows and the horses fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: In the fight the Turks were hemmed in. The Xueyantuo sprang up to chase them. Li Ji rushed to their aid. The Xueyantuo shot volleys and horses dropped dead.

sentences.zh: 勣乃以步士百人為隊，搗其罅，虜潰，部將薛萬徹率勁騎先收執馬者，故延陀不能去，斬首數千級，獲馬萬五千。

translations.literal: Li Ji then formed infantry in companies of a hundred and drove into their gaps. The barbarians broke. Subordinate general Xue Wanche led crack cavalry to seize first those who held the horses, so the Xueyantuo could not flee. Several thousand heads were cut off and fifteen thousand horses taken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji formed foot soldiers in hundreds and punched through their gaps. The tribes broke. Xue Wanche led elite cavalry to seize the horse-holders first, so the Xueyantuo could not escape. Several thousand heads were taken and fifteen thousand horses captured.

sentences.zh: 大度設亡去，萬徹追弗及。

translations.literal: Dadu She fled. Wanche pursued but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Dadu She escaped. Wanche chased but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 殘卒奔漠北，會雪甚，眾皸踣死者十八。

translations.literal: The broken troops fled north of the desert. Heavy snow came; eighteen in ten of the multitude froze or fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled north of the desert. Snow fell thick; eight or nine in ten froze or fell dead on the road.

sentences.zh: 始延陀能以術禬神致雪，冀困勣師，及是反自敝雲。

translations.literal: At first the Xueyantuo could use ritual to pray to the spirits and bring snow, hoping to trap Li Ji's army. Now it turned and harmed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo had once prayed to the spirits for snow to trap Li Ji's army. Now the snow destroyed them instead.

sentences.zh: 勣還入定襄，天子遣使者賫璽書勞問，賞功恤死。

translations.literal: Li Ji returned and entered Dingxiang. The Son of Heaven sent envoys bearing sealed edicts to comfort and inquire, rewarding merit and comforting the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji returned to Dingxiang. The emperor sent envoys with sealed letters of praise, rewarding the living and comforting the fallen.

sentences.zh: 延陀之使留待命者，帝悉還之，曰：「歸語爾可汗，爾自負其強，以突厥為弱，厚誅斂之，又取首領以為質，且我為天下主，渠嘗賦發於爾邪？

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo envoys left behind awaiting orders—the emperor sent them all back, saying: "Return and tell your qaghan: you relied on your strength, took the Turks for weak, levied them heavily, and took their chiefs as hostages. Yet I am lord of all under heaven—when did I ever levy tribute on you?
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo envoys still waiting at court were all sent home. The emperor said, "Tell your qaghan: you trusted your strength, thought the Turks weak, taxed them harshly, and took their leaders hostage. I am lord of all under heaven—when did I ever tax you?

sentences.zh: 後有利害，當謹思，毋遽也。」

translations.literal: Hereafter, when profit and harm are at stake, think carefully—do not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When gain and loss come again, think hard—do not be hasty.

sentences.zh: 延陀乃遣使謝罪，又遣其仲父沙缽羅獻馬三千，因請昏。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo then sent envoys to apologize and also sent his uncle Shaboluo with three thousand horses, requesting marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo sent envoys to apologize and his uncle Shaboluo with three thousand horses to ask for a princess.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「延陀本一俟斤，我則立之，度其力孰與頡利比，而敢橈邊乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Xueyantuo were only one irkin—I raised them up. How does their strength compare with Jieli's, that they dare trouble the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Xueyantuo were only one irkin clan—I made them qaghan. How do they compare with Jieli, that they dare harass the border?

sentences.zh: 不許昏。

translations.literal: Marriage was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The marriage was refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，以使來益獻馬、牛、羊、橐它，固求昏。

translations.literal: The next year envoys came bringing still more horses, cattle, sheep, and camels, firmly requesting marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they sent envoys with still more horses, cattle, sheep, and camels, pressing again for marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝與大臣計曰：「延陀屈強，朕策顧有二：選士十萬擊之，使無遺種，百年計也；

translations.literal: The emperor consulted his ministers, saying: "The Xueyantuo are stubborn and strong. My plans have two: select one hundred thousand troops to strike them and leave no seed—a plan for a hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers, "The Xueyantuo are proud and strong. I see two courses: raise a hundred thousand men, crush them root and branch—a hundred-year plan;

sentences.zh: 絕昏羈縻，使無邊憂，三十年計也。

translations.literal: refuse marriage and keep them on reins, leaving no frontier worry—a thirty-year plan.
translations.idiomatic: or refuse the marriage and hold them on reins, free of frontier trouble for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 然則孰利？」

translations.literal: Which then is more profitable?
translations.idiomatic: Which pays better?

sentences.zh: 房玄齡曰：「今大亂余氓，痍破未完，戰雖勝，猶危道也。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling said: "Now the people are survivors of great disorder, wounded and not yet whole. Even victory in war is still a perilous path.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said, "The people are still survivors of chaos, wounded and not yet healed. Even victory in war is a dangerous road.

sentences.zh: 不如和親。」

translations.literal: It is better to seek peace by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Better to make peace through marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well spoken."

sentences.zh: 許以新興公主下嫁，召突利失大享，群臣侍，陳寶器，奏《慶善》、《破陣》盛樂及十部伎，突利失頓首上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: He agreed to send down Princess Xinxing in marriage and summoned Tuli Shi to a great feast. The ministers attended. Precious vessels were displayed. The music "Qingshan" and "Pozhen," splendid performances, and the ten-department entertainers were played. Tuli Shi bowed his head and wished the emperor ten thousand years of life.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed to marry Princess Xinxing to them and summoned Tuli Shi to a grand banquet. Ministers attended; treasure was displayed; "Qingshan," "Pozhen," splendid music, and the ten-department players performed. Tuli Shi bowed and wished the emperor ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 詔夷男親迎，帝將幸靈州以成昏事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi Nan to come in person to welcome the bride. The emperor would travel to Lingzhou to complete the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Nan was ordered to come in person to fetch the bride. The emperor would go to Lingzhou to seal the marriage.

sentences.zh: 夷男大喜，詫曰：「我鐵勒部人耳，上以我為可汗，公主以女我，乘輿為我幸邊，誰與我榮？」

translations.literal: Yi Nan was greatly pleased and exclaimed: "I am only a man of the Tiele tribes. The emperor made me qaghan, gave me his daughter in marriage, and will himself travel to the frontier for my sake—who shares such glory with me?
translations.idiomatic: Yi Nan was overjoyed. "I am only a Tiele tribesman," he cried. "The Son of Heaven made me qaghan, gave me his daughter, and will ride to the frontier for me—who else has such honor?

sentences.zh: 乃搜賦諸下羊馬為貲。

translations.literal: He then levied sheep and horses from his followers as bride-price.
translations.idiomatic: He levied sheep and horses from his people for the bride-price.

sentences.zh: 或說夷男曰：「可汗與唐，皆一國主，奈何往朝？

translations.literal: Some urged Yi Nan: "The qaghan and Tang are both rulers of a state—why go to court?
translations.idiomatic: Some told Yi Nan, "You and Tang are both sovereigns—why go to court?

sentences.zh: 有如見款，尚可悔？」

translations.literal: If you are received with courtesy, can you still regret it?
translations.idiomatic: If they receive you as a guest, can you still turn back?

sentences.zh: 夷男曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Yi Nan said: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Nan said, "No.

sentences.zh: 吾聞唐天子有德，四方共臣之，借獨留我，磧北亦須有主，然舍我而求它，非計也。」

translations.literal: I have heard that the Tang Son of Heaven has virtue and that the four quarters all serve him as subjects. If he alone kept me back, there would still have to be a lord north of the desert—but to leave me and seek another would not be a sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the Tang emperor is virtuous and all the world serves him. Even if he kept only me, someone would still rule north of the desert—but to cast me aside for another would be folly.

sentences.zh: 下乃不敢言。

translations.literal: His followers then dared not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: His men dared say no more.

sentences.zh: 時帝詔有司受所獻，延陀無府庫，調斂於下，不亟集，又度磧，水草乏，馬羊多死，納貢後期，帝亦止行。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had ordered the authorities to receive their gifts. The Xueyantuo had no treasury and levied from below; the collection was not swift. They also crossed the desert; grass and water were scarce and many horses and sheep died. The tribute was late, and the emperor also canceled his journey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered officials to receive their gifts. The Xueyantuo had no treasury and taxed their people; the levy came in slowly. Crossing the desert, fodder failed and half their herds died. Tribute arrived late, and the emperor canceled the journey.

sentences.zh: 畜口耗死僅半，議者謂：「夷狄嘗為中國私，今禮不具而與昏，恐後有輕中國心。」

translations.literal: Advisers said: "Barbarians have often been China's servants. Now the rites are not complete yet marriage is granted—I fear that later they will look lightly on China.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said, "Barbarians have long been China's servants. To marry before the rites are complete may teach them to despise the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔絕昏，謝其使。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued breaking off the marriage and apologizing to their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: An edict broke off the marriage and dismissed their envoys with regrets.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「既許之，信不可失。」

translations.literal: Some said: "Since it was promised, faith must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged, "A promise was given—faith cannot be broken.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公等計非也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your plans are mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are wrong.

sentences.zh: 昔漢匈奴強，中國不抗，故飾子女嫁單於。

translations.literal: In former times the Han Xiongnu were strong and China could not resist them, so they adorned daughters to marry the chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the Xiongnu were strong and China could not match them, so they dressed up daughters for the chanyu.

sentences.zh: 今北狄弱，我能制之，而延陀方謹事我者，顧新立，倚我以服眾。

translations.literal: Now the northern Di are weak and I can control them. The Xueyantuo are scrupulous in serving me only because they have just been established and rely on me to bring the masses to heel.
translations.idiomatic: Now the northern tribes are weak and I can master them. The Xueyantuo serve me carefully only because they are newly raised and lean on me to rule their people.

sentences.zh: 彼同羅、仆骨力足制延陀而不發，懼我也。

translations.literal: The Tongluo and Pugu have strength enough to crush the Xueyantuo yet do not move—they fear me.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo and Pugu could destroy the Xueyantuo yet hold back—they fear me.

sentences.zh: 我又妻之，固中國婿，名重而援堅，諸部將歸之，戎狄野心，能自立則叛矣。

translations.literal: If I also marry them, I would firmly be China's son-in-law—name weighty and support solid—and the tribes would turn to them. Barbarian hearts are wild; once they can stand alone they rebel.
translations.idiomatic: If I wed them too, I become their son-in-law in earnest—honor and backing fused—and the tribes would flock to them. Barbarian hearts are restless; give them strength and they rebel.

sentences.zh: 今絕昏，使諸姓聞之，將爭擊延陀，亡可待也。」

translations.literal: Now, breaking off the marriage, let the various clans hear of it—they will compete to strike the Xueyantuo, and their destruction waits on no delay.
translations.idiomatic: Break the marriage and let every clan hear—they will rush to strike the Xueyantuo, and their end needs no long wait.

sentences.zh: 李思摩果侵掠之。

translations.literal: Li Simo indeed raided and plundered them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Simo did raid them at once.

sentences.zh: 延陀遣突利失寇定襄，詔李勣逐出塞。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo sent Tuli Shi to raid Dingxiang. An edict ordered Li Ji to drive them beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo sent Tuli Shi against Dingxiang. Li Ji was ordered to drive them out of the passes.

sentences.zh: 俄遣使請率師助伐高麗，以刺帝意，帝引使者謂曰：「歸語爾可汗，我父子東征，能寇邊者可即來。」

translations.literal: Soon they sent envoys asking to lead troops to help attack Goguryeo, to probe the emperor's mind. The emperor led the envoys forward and said: "Return and tell your qaghan: my father and I are campaigning east. Whoever wishes to raid the frontier may come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they sent envoys offering troops against Goguryeo, testing the emperor's mood. He brought the envoys forward and said, "Tell your qaghan: my father and I march east. Let whoever wants to raid the border come now.

sentences.zh: 夷男沮縮，不敢謀，以使謝，固請助軍。

translations.literal: Yi Nan shrank back in dismay, dared not plot further, sent envoys to apologize, and firmly asked to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Nan shrank back in alarm, dared plot no more, apologized by envoy, and pressed again to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉答。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted.

sentences.zh: 高麗莫離支令靺鞨以厚利啖夷男，欲與連和，夷男氣素索，不發，亦會病死，帝為祭於行。

translations.literal: Goguryeo's Molichi ordered the Mohe to entice Yi Nan with rich profit, wishing to join in alliance. Yi Nan's spirit had always been frail and he did not act. He also happened to fall ill and die. The emperor performed sacrifice for him on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo's Molichi sent Mohe to tempt Yi Nan with rich gifts and win an alliance. Yi Nan had always been timid and did not stir. He fell ill and died besides. The emperor offered sacrifice for him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 始延陀請以庶子曳莽為突利失可汗，統東方；

translations.literal: At first the Xueyantuo had asked to make the secondary son Yemang Tuli Shi qaghan to rule the east;
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo had first asked to make the younger son Yemang Tuli Shi qaghan of the east;

sentences.zh: 嫡子拔灼為肆葉護可汗，統西方。

translations.literal: the eldest son Bazhuo Siyehu qaghan to rule the west.
translations.idiomatic: and the eldest son Bazhuo Siyehu qaghan of the west.

sentences.zh: 白道之役，曳莽實為之謀，國人多怨。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Baidao, Yemang had in fact devised the plan; many in the state resented it.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Baidao, Yemang had actually masterminded the campaign, and resentment ran deep among his people.

sentences.zh: 及會葬，曳莽亟還部，拔灼分兵襲殺之，自立為頡利俱利失薛沙多彌可汗。

translations.literal: When they gathered for the funeral, Yemang hurried back to his division; Bazhuo split off troops in a surprise attack and killed him, then installed himself as Jieli Juli Shixueshaduomi qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral assembly Yemang rushed back to his own division, but Bazhuo detached forces in a surprise attack and killed him, then proclaimed himself Jieli Juli Shixueshaduomi qaghan.

sentences.zh: 方是時，王師猶在遼，因即寇邊。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army was still in Liaodong, so he immediately raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: With the imperial forces still campaigning in Liaodong, he seized the moment to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝遣江夏王道宗屯朔州，代州都督薛萬徹與左驍衛大將軍阿史那社爾屯勝州，左武候大將軍薩孤吳仁屯靈州，執失思力與突厥掎角塞下，虜知有備，乃去。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Prince Daizong of Jiangxia to garrison Shuozhou; Surveillance Commissioner for Daizhou Xue Wanche and Left Guard Grand General Ashina She'er garrisoned Shengzhou; Left Wuwei General Sadokuren garrisoned Lingzhou; Zhisi Sili and the Turks held the frontier in pincer formation. Learning there were preparations, the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Prince Daizong of Jiangxia to hold Shuozhou; Xue Wanche, surveillance commissioner for Daizhou, and Left Guard grand general Ashina She'er to hold Shengzhou; Left Wuwei grand general Sadokuren to hold Lingzhou; and Zhisi Sili to coordinate with the Turks in a pincer along the frontier. When the enemy saw the border was ready, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 拔灼性卞克，多殺父時貴臣而任所親昵，國人不安，而阿波設與唐使者遇於靺鞨東鄙，小戰不利，還怖國人曰：「唐兵至矣！」

translations.literal: Bazhuo was impulsive and harsh; he killed many noble ministers from his father's time and relied on his own favorites, so the people were uneasy. Apo She met Tang envoys on the eastern fringe of Mohe; after a minor defeat he returned and frightened his people, saying: "Tang troops have arrived!
translations.idiomatic: Bazhuo was violent and severe. He killed many eminent ministers from his father's reign and entrusted power only to men he favored, leaving the realm unsettled. Apo She encountered Tang envoys on Mohe's eastern marches and, after a small reverse, returned to terrify his people with the cry: "The Tang army is upon us!

sentences.zh: 眾大擾，諸部遂潰。

translations.literal: The masses were greatly disturbed, and the various divisions scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the ranks, and the tribes broke apart in flight.

sentences.zh: 多彌可汗以十餘騎遁去，依阿史那時健，俄為回紇所殺，盡屠其宗，眾五六萬奔西域，立真珠毗伽可汗昆弟子咄摩支，號伊特勿失可汗，遣使者上言：「願保郁督軍山。」

translations.literal: Duomi qaghan fled with a dozen or so horsemen, relying on Ashina Shijian; soon he was killed by the Huihe, who slaughtered his entire clan. Fifty or sixty thousand fled to the Western Regions, enthroning Zhenzhu Pijia qaghan Kun's nephew Duomozhi as Yite Wushi qaghan, and sent envoys saying: "We wish to hold Yudujunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Duomi qaghan escaped with little more than a dozen riders and threw himself on Ashina Shijian's protection, but the Huihe soon killed him and exterminated his house. Some fifty or sixty thousand fled west, set up Zhenzhu Pijia qaghan Kun's nephew Duomozhi as Yite Wushi qaghan, and sent envoys to say: "We ask to keep Yudujunshan.

sentences.zh: 常詔兵部尚書崔敦禮與李勣尉安之，俾定其國。

translations.literal: The court regularly ordered Minister of War Cui Dunli and Li Ji to pacify and settle them and help fix their state.
translations.idiomatic: The court routinely charged Minister of War Cui Dunli and Li Ji with pacifying them and helping settle their polity.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒諸部素伏延陀，而咄摩支雖衰孑，尚臣畏之。

translations.literal: The Tiele tribes had long submitted to the Xueyantuo, and though Duomozhi was but a remnant, they still feared and obeyed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele peoples had long bowed to the Xueyantuo, and even in his weakened state Duomozhi still commanded their awe.

sentences.zh: 帝恐卒為患，詔勣等曰：「降則撫之，叛則擊之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor feared he might suddenly become a threat and ordered Li Ji and the others: "If they submit, comfort them; if they rebel, strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he might yet become a sudden menace, the emperor instructed Li Ji and his colleagues: "Comfort those who surrender; attack those who resist.

sentences.zh: 勣至，咄摩支大駭，陰欲拒戰，外好言乞降。

translations.literal: When Li Ji arrived, Duomozhi was greatly alarmed and secretly intended to resist, while outwardly speaking warmly of begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji's arrival threw Duomozhi into terror. He plotted resistance in secret even as he spoke meekly of submission.

sentences.zh: 勣知之，縱兵擊，斬五千餘級，系老孺三萬，遂滅其國。

translations.literal: Li Ji learned of this, unleashed his troops in attack, beheaded more than five thousand, seized old and young numbering thirty thousand, and thereupon destroyed their state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji saw through the ruse, attacked in force, took more than five thousand heads, captured thirty thousand old and young, and extinguished the regime.

sentences.zh: 咄摩支聞天子使者蕭嗣業在回紇，身詣嗣業丐降，入朝，拜右武衛將軍，賜田宅。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Son of Heaven's envoy Xiao Siye was among the Huihe, Duomozhi went in person to beg surrender from Siye, entered court, and was appointed Right Martial Guard general with grants of fields and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the emperor's envoy Xiao Siye was with the Huihe, Duomozhi went to him in person to beg mercy, then came to court and was made Right Martial Guard general with lands and a residence.

sentences.zh: 初，延陀將滅，有丐食於其部者，延客帳中，妻視客人而狼首，主不覺，客已食，妻語部人共追之，至郁督軍山，見二人焉，曰：「我神也，薛延陀且滅。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Xueyantuo were on the verge of destruction, a man begging food in their camp was received in the chief's tent; the wife saw the guest had a wolf's head, but the host did not notice. After the guest had eaten, the wife told the tribesmen to pursue him together. At Yudujunshan they saw two men who said: "We are spirits; the Xueyantuo will soon perish.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Xueyantuo fell, a beggar was entertained in a chieftain's tent. The wife saw the visitor's head was that of a wolf, though her husband did not. After the man had eaten, she urged the tribe to pursue him. At Yudujunshan they came upon two figures who declared: "We are divine beings; the Xueyantuo are about to be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 追者懼，卻走，遂失之。

translations.literal: The pursuers were afraid and retreated, and so lost them.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers fled in fear and lost the trail.

sentences.zh: 至是果敗此山下。

translations.literal: Now they were indeed defeated below this mountain.
translations.idiomatic: And now, as foretold, they were broken on that very mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝以延陀滅，欲並契等降之，復遣道宗率阿史那社爾等分部窮討，帝幸靈州，節度諸將。

translations.literal: With the Xueyantuo destroyed, the Emperor wished to bring the Qi and others to submission as well, and again sent Daozong leading Ashina She'er and others in divisions to pursue them to the end; the Emperor went in person to Lingzhou to direct the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Xueyantuo were gone, the emperor sought to bring the Qi and other tribes under control as well. He again sent Daozong with Ashina She'er and others in separate columns to hunt down the remnants, while he himself went to Lingzhou to command the armies.

sentences.zh: 於是鐵勒十一部皆歸命天子，請吏內屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon all eleven Tiele tribes submitted to the Son of Heaven and asked to be governed and brought within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: All eleven Tiele tribes then pledged themselves to the Son of Heaven and petitioned for officials and incorporation within the empire.

sentences.zh: 道宗等徑磧擊延陀餘眾阿波達幹，斬首千餘級，逐北二百里。

translations.literal: Daozong and the others struck straight across the desert at the Xueyantuo remnant Apodagan, beheading more than a thousand and pursuing north two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong and his forces crossed the desert directly against the Xueyantuo remnant Apodagan, taking more than a thousand heads and driving the enemy two hundred li north.

sentences.zh: 萬徹抵北道，諭降回紇諸酋。

translations.literal: Xue Wanche reached the northern route and persuaded the Huihe chieftains to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanche advanced along the northern road and won the submission of the Huihe chiefs.

sentences.zh: 虜所遣使踵及帝行在，凡數千人，上言：「天至尊為可汗，世世以奴事，死不恨。」

translations.literal: Envoys sent by the barbarians caught up with the Emperor's traveling camp one after another, several thousand in all, saying: "May the Heavenly Sovereign be our qaghan; generation after generation we will serve as slaves—we would not regret death.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian envoys followed the emperor's camp in unbroken succession, thousands in all, declaring: "Let the Heavenly Sovereign be our qaghan; for generation upon generation we will serve as your slaves and die without regret.

sentences.zh: 帝剖其地為州縣，北荒遂平。

translations.literal: The Emperor carved their lands into prefectures and counties, and the northern wilds were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor divided their territory into prefectures and counties, and the northern frontier was at last quiet.

sentences.zh: 諸姓有來朝者，帝勞曰：「爾來，若鼠得穴、魚得泉，我為爾深廣之。」

translations.literal: When clansmen came to court, the Emperor comforted them, saying: "You have come as a mouse finds a hole or a fish finds a spring—I will broaden and deepen it for you.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal leaders arrived at court, the emperor reassured them: "You have come as a mouse finds its burrow or a fish its spring; I will make that refuge wider and deeper for you.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「我在，天下四夷有不安安之，不樂樂之，如驥尾受蒼蠅，可使日千里也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "While I live, if any of the four barbarians of the world are not secure, I will secure them; if they are not content, I will content them—as a swift horse's tail may bear flies yet still run a thousand li in a day."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "So long as I reign, wherever the four quarters are uneasy I will give them peace; wherever they are unhappy I will give them joy—like a thoroughbred whose tail attracts flies yet still flies a thousand li in a day."

sentences.zh: 於是告功太廟，賜民三日酺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reported the achievement in the Grand Ancestral Temple and granted the people three days of communal feasting.
translations.idiomatic: He then announced the victory in the Grand Ancestral Temple and granted the people three days of public rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 後三年，餘部叛，以右領軍大將軍執失思力討平之。

translations.literal: Three years later the remnant tribes rebelled; Right Guard Grand General Zhisi Sili was sent to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, scattered remnants rebelled, and Right Guard grand general Zhisi Sili was dispatched to crush them.

sentences.zh: 至永徽時，延陀部亡散者悉還，高宗為置奚彈州處安之。

translations.literal: By the Yonghui era, all the scattered Xueyantuo who had fled had returned; Gaozong established the Xi Tan prefecture to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yonghui period every Xueyantuo refugee had come back, and Emperor Gaozong established Xi Tan prefecture to receive them.

sentences.zh: 拔野古一曰拔野固，或為拔曳固，漫散磧北，地千里，直仆骨東，鄰於靺鞨。

translations.literal: Bayegu was also called Bayegu, or Bayegu; they were scattered north of the desert over a thousand li, directly east of the Pugu and bordering the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: The Bayegu—also written Bayegu or Bayegu—were spread across a thousand li north of the desert, due east of the Pugu and adjacent to the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 帳戶六萬，兵萬人。

translations.literal: Tents numbered sixty thousand; troops, ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They had sixty thousand tents and ten thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 地有薦草，產良馬、精鐵。

translations.literal: The land had fine pasture grass and produced excellent horses and refined iron.
translations.idiomatic: Their country offered good grazing, fine horses, and quality iron.

sentences.zh: 有川曰康幹河，斷松投之，三年輒化為石，色蒼致，然節理猶在，世謂康幹石者。

translations.literal: There was a river called the Kanggan; pine thrown into it would in three years turn to stone, dark blue in color, yet the grain of the wood remained—what the world calls Kanggan stone.
translations.idiomatic: A stream called the Kanggan was said to petrify pine cast into it within three years into dark blue stone that still showed the wood's grain—the so-called Kanggan stone.

sentences.zh: 俗嗜獵射，少耕獲，乘木逐鹿冰上。

translations.literal: Their custom favored hunting and archery; they did little farming, and rode logs to chase deer on the ice.
translations.idiomatic: They lived by the hunt and the bow, sowed little, and on ice would slide on logs to run down deer.

sentences.zh: 風俗大抵鐵勒也，言語少異。

translations.literal: Their ways were largely those of the Tiele, with only slight differences in speech.
translations.idiomatic: In custom they were much like the other Tiele, with only minor differences of language.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，與仆骨、同羅、奚、霫同入朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan they entered court together with the Pugu, Tongluo, Xi, and Xi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 they came to court alongside the Pugu, Tongluo, Xi, and Xi peoples.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，大俟利發屈利失舉部內屬，置幽陵都督府，拜屈利失右武衛大將軍，即為都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Grand Irkin Qulishi led his tribe to submit; the Youling Protectorate was established, Qulishi was appointed Right Martial Guard grand general and made its protector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 the grand irkin Qulishi brought his people in; the Youling Protectorate was set up, and Qulishi was made Right Martial Guard grand general and protector.

sentences.zh: 顯慶時，與思結、仆固、同羅叛，以左武衛大將軍鄭仁泰擊之，斬其渠首。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era they rebelled together with the Sijie, Pugu, and Tongluo; Left Martial Guard grand general Zheng Rentai attacked them and beheaded their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing they rose with the Sijie, Pugu, and Tongluo; Left Martial Guard grand general Zheng Rentai defeated them and slew their chiefs.

sentences.zh: 至天寶間，能自來朝。

translations.literal: By the Tianbao period they were again able to come to court on their own.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianbao reign they were once more coming to court of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 仆骨亦曰仆固，在多覽葛之東。

translations.literal: The Pugu were also called Pugu and lived east of the Duolange.
translations.idiomatic: The Pugu—also called Pugu—dwelt east of the Duolange.

sentences.zh: 帳戶三萬，兵萬人。

translations.literal: Tents numbered thirty thousand; troops, ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They had thirty thousand tents and ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 地最北，俗梗驁，難召率。

translations.literal: Their land was the farthest north; the people were stubborn and proud, hard to summon and lead.
translations.idiomatic: They held the northernmost territory; proud and unyielding, they were difficult to command.

sentences.zh: 始臣突厥，後附薛延陀。

translations.literal: They first served the Turks, then attached themselves to the Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: They had first submitted to the Turks, then to the Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 延陀滅，其酋娑匐俟利發歌濫拔延始內屬，以其地為金微州，拜歌濫拔延為右武衛大將軍、州都督。

translations.literal: When the Xueyantuo perished, their chief Sabo Irkin Gelan Bayan first submitted; their land was made Jinwei prefecture, and Gelan Bayan was appointed Right Martial Guard grand general and prefectural protector.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xueyantuo fell, their chief Sabo irkin Gelan Bayan led them in; their territory became Jinwei prefecture, and Gelan Bayan was named Right Martial Guard grand general and protector.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為首領仆固所殺，詣朔方降，有司誅之。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era he was killed by the chieftain Pugu, who then surrendered at Shuofang and was executed by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan a chieftain named Pugu killed him; he went to Shuofang to surrender and was put to death by the court.

sentences.zh: 子曰懷恩，至德時以功至朔方節度使，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son was Huai'en, who in the Zhide era rose to Shuofang military commissioner on merit and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai'en later became Shuofang military commissioner for his achievements in the Zhide era and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 同羅在薛延陀北，多覽葛之東，距京師七千里而贏，勝兵三萬。

translations.literal: The Tongluo lay north of the Xueyantuo and east of the Duolange, seven thousand li from the capital by the longer route, with thirty thousand effectives.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo lived north of the Xueyantuo and east of the Duolange, seven thousand li from the capital by the circuitous road, with thirty thousand men under arms.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan they sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 they dispatched envoys to the court.

sentences.zh: 久之，請內屬，置龜林都督府，拜酋俟利發時健啜為左領軍大將軍，即授都督。

translations.literal: After a long interval they asked to submit; the Guilin Protectorate was established, and Irkin Shijian Chuo of the tribe was appointed Left Guard grand general and made protector.
translations.idiomatic: Years later they sought incorporation; the Guilin Protectorate was founded, and tribal irkin Shijian Chuo was made Left Guard grand general and protector.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，劫其兵用之，號「曳落河」者也。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled he seized their troops for his use—they were the so-called "yeluohe."
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion he impressed their warriors—the force known as the "yeluohe."

sentences.zh: 曳落河，猶言健兒雲。

translations.literal: Yeluohe means something like "stalwart youths."
translations.idiomatic: "Yeluohe" means, roughly, "hardy fighters."

sentences.zh: 渾在諸部最南者。

translations.literal: The Hun were the southernmost of all these tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the tribes, the Hun lay farthest south.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利敗時，有俟利發阿貪支款塞。

translations.literal: When Turkish qaghan Jieli was defeated, Irkin Aganzhi came to the frontier to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of the Turkish qaghan Jieli, irkin Aganzhi presented himself at the border to surrender.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀之滅，大俟利發渾汪舉部內向，以其地為臯蘭都督府，後分東、西州。

translations.literal: When the Xueyantuo fell, Grand Irkin Hun Wang led his tribe inward; their land was made the Gaolan Protectorate, later divided into eastern and western prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of the Xueyantuo, grand irkin Hun Wang brought his people in; their territory became the Gaolan Protectorate, later split into eastern and western commands.

sentences.zh: 太宗以阿貪支於汪屬尊，遣譯者諷汪，汪欣然避位。

translations.literal: Because Aganzhi was senior within Wang's following, Taizong sent an interpreter to hint to Wang, and Wang gladly yielded his place.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, holding Aganzhi the senior man in Wang's following, had an interpreter suggest that Wang step aside, and Wang did so willingly.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其讓，以阿貪支為右領軍衛大將軍、臯蘭州刺史，汪雲麾將軍兼俟利發為之副。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his deference, appointed Aganzhi Right Guard grand general and Gaolan prefect, and made Wang Cloud-Banner general and vice irkin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his humility, made Aganzhi Right Guard grand general and Gaolan prefect, and named Wang Cloud-Banner general with the title of vice irkin.

sentences.zh: 阿貪支死，子回貴嗣。

translations.literal: Aganzhi died and his son Huigui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Aganzhi died; his son Huigui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 回貴死，子大壽嗣。

translations.literal: Huigui died and his son Dashou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Huigui died; his son Dashou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大壽死，子釋之嗣。

translations.literal: Dashou died and his son Shizhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou died; his son Shizhi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 釋之鷙勇不凡，從哥舒翰拔石堡城，遷右武衛大將軍，封汝南郡公。

translations.literal: Shizhi was fierce and brave beyond the common run; following Geshu Han he took Shibao fortress and was promoted to Right Martial Guard grand general and enfeoffed Duke of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was a man of uncommon fierceness and courage. Serving under Geshu Han he captured Shibao fortress, rose to Right Martial Guard grand general, and was enfeoffed Duke of Runan.

sentences.zh: 李光弼保河陽，釋之以朔方都知兵馬使為裨將，進寧朔郡王，知朔方節度留後。

translations.literal: When Li Guangbi held Heyang, Shizhi served as deputy under the Shuofang army inspector, was advanced to Prince of Ningshuo, and acted as deputy military commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangbi defended Heyang, Shizhi became his deputy as Shuofang army inspector, was raised to Prince of Ningshuo, and served as acting Shuofang military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩之走，聲為歸鎮。

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en fled, he gave out that he was returning to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en broke away, he claimed he was merely going back to his post.

sentences.zh: 釋之曰：「是必眾潰。」

translations.literal: Shizhi said: "This can only mean the host has broken in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi said: "That can only mean his men have scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 將拒之，其甥張韶曰：「彼如悔禍還鎮，渠可不納？」

translations.literal: As he was about to refuse entry, his nephew Zhang Shao said: "If he truly repents and returns to his command, how can you not receive him?"
translations.idiomatic: He was on the point of barring the gates when his nephew Zhang Shao argued: "If he has repented and is truly returning to his post, how can you turn him away?"

sentences.zh: 釋之信之，乃納懷恩。

translations.literal: Shizhi believed him and admitted Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi trusted the advice and let Huai'en in.

sentences.zh: 懷恩已入，使韶殺釋之，收其軍。

translations.literal: Once inside, Huai'en had Shao kill Shizhi and seized his army.
translations.idiomatic: Once within, Huai'en set Shao to kill Shizhi and took control of the army.

sentences.zh: 已而惡韶，罵曰：「若負舅，肯忠於我？」

translations.literal: Soon he came to hate Shao and cursed him: "If you could betray your uncle, would you be loyal to me?
translations.idiomatic: Before long he turned on Shao and reviled him: "Betray your uncle—would you then be faithful to me?

sentences.zh: 折其脛，囚死彌峨城。

translations.literal: He broke Shao's shins and imprisoned him until he died at Mie'e city.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Shao's legs and kept him imprisoned until he died at Mie'e.

sentences.zh: 釋之子瑊，建中功臣也，自有傳。

translations.literal: Shizhi's son Jian was a hero of the Jianzhong era and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi's son Jian became a noted champion of the Jianzhong period and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 契亦曰契羽，在焉耆西北鷹娑川，多覽葛之南。

translations.literal: The Qi were also called Qiyu; they lived on the Yingcha River northwest of Kucha, south of the Duolange.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi—also called Qiyu—dwelt on the Yingcha River northwest of Kucha, south of the Duolange.

sentences.zh: 其酋哥楞自號易勿真莫賀可汗，弟莫賀咄特勒，皆有勇。

translations.literal: Their chief Geling styled himself Yiwu Zhen Mohe qaghan; his younger brother Moheduo tegin were both men of courage.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Geling took the title Yiwu Zhen Mohe qaghan; his younger brother Moheduo tegin was likewise a warrior of note.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄死，子何力尚紐率其部來歸，時貞觀六年也。

translations.literal: When Moheduo died, his son Heli Shangniu led the tribe to submit; this was in the sixth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: After Moheduo's death his son Heli Shangniu brought the tribe in—this was Zhenguan 6.

sentences.zh: 詔處之甘、涼間，以其地為榆溪州。

translations.literal: They were ordered settled between Gan and Liang, and their land was made Yuxi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court settled them between Gan and Liang and organized their territory as Yuxi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，以其部為賀蘭都督府，隸燕然都護。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui their tribe was made the Helan Protectorate, subordinate to the Yanran Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 4 their people were organized as the Helan Protectorate under the Yanran Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 何力有戰功，忠節臣也。

translations.literal: Heli had military achievements and was a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Heli won distinction in battle and proved a steadfast servant of the throne.

sentences.zh: 大和中，其種帳附於振武雲。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era their tribal registers attached to Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dahe period their tribal registers were attached to Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 多覽葛亦曰多濫，在薛延陀東，濱同羅水，勝兵萬人。

translations.literal: The Duolange were also called Duolan; they lay east of the Xueyantuo on the Tongluo River, with ten thousand effectives.
translations.idiomatic: The Duolange—also Duolan—lived east of the Xueyantuo along the Tongluo River with ten thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 延陀已滅，其酋俟斤多濫葛末與回紇皆朝，以其地為燕然都督府，授右衛大將軍，即為府都督。

translations.literal: After the Xueyantuo were destroyed, their chief Irkin Duolangemo came to court together with the Huihe; their land was made the Yanran Protectorate, and he was appointed Right Guard grand general and made protector.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Xueyantuo were gone, irkin Duolangemo of the tribe came to court with the Huihe; Yanran Protectorate was established, and he was made Right Guard grand general and protector.

sentences.zh: 死，以多濫葛塞匐為大俟利發，繼為都督。

translations.literal: When he died, Duolangemo Saifu was made grand irkin and succeeded as protector.
translations.idiomatic: On his death Duolangemo Saifu became grand irkin and protector in his stead.

sentences.zh: 阿跌，亦曰訶咥，或為跌。

translations.literal: The Adie were also called Hezhi, or written Die.
translations.idiomatic: The Adie were also called Hezhi, sometimes written simply Die.

sentences.zh: 始與拔野古等皆朝，以其地為雞田州。

translations.literal: At first they came to court together with the Bayegu and others; their land was made Jitian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They first presented themselves at court with the Bayegu and others, and their territory was organized as Jitian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元中，跌思泰自突厥默啜所來降。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Diesitai came in surrender from the Turkish qaghan Mokusho.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan Diesitai defected from the Turkish qaghan Mokusho.

sentences.zh: 其後，光進、光顏皆以戰功至大官，賜李氏，附屬籍，自有傳。

translations.literal: Later, Guangjin and Guangyan both rose to high office through military merit, were granted the surname Li, entered the household registers, and have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guangjin and Guangyan both reached high rank through battlefield service, received the imperial surname Li, were entered on the registers, and are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 葛邏祿本突厥諸族，在北庭西北、金山之西，跨仆固振水，包多怛嶺，與車鼻部接。

translations.literal: The Geluolu were originally a Turkish people, northwest of Beiting and west of the Altai, spanning the Pugu's Zhenshui and enclosing the Duoduling, adjoining the Chebi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Geluolu were originally a Turkish people living northwest of Beiting and west of the Altai, straddling the Pugu's Zhenshui and the Duoduling range, bordering the Chebi tribes.

sentences.zh: 有三族：一謀落，或為謀刺；

translations.literal: They had three clans: first, Moluo, also called Moci;
translations.idiomatic: They comprised three clans: the Moluo, also called Moci;

sentences.zh: 二熾俟，或為婆匐；

translations.literal: second, Chishi, also called Pofu;
translations.idiomatic: the Chishi, also called Pofu;

sentences.zh: 三踏實力。

translations.literal: third, Tashili.
translations.idiomatic: and the Tashili.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，高偘之伐車鼻可汗，三族皆內屬。

translations.literal: In the early Yonghui era, when Gao Kan campaigned against Qaghan Chebi, all three clans submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yonghui, when Gao Kan attacked Qaghan Chebi, all three submitted.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，以謀落部為陰山都督府，熾俟部為大漠都督府，踏實力部為玄池都督府，即用其酋長為都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing the Moluo were made the Yinshan Protectorate, the Chishi the Damo Protectorate, and the Tashili the Xuanchi Protectorate, their chieftains appointed protectors.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 the Moluo became the Yinshan Protectorate, the Chishi the Damo Protectorate, and the Tashili the Xuanchi Protectorate, each under its own chieftain as protector.

sentences.zh: 後分熾俟部置金附州。

translations.literal: Later the Chishi division was further split to establish Jinfu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later a separate Jinfu prefecture was carved from the Chishi branch.

sentences.zh: 三族當東、西突厥間，常視其興衰，附叛不常也。

translations.literal: The three clans lay between Eastern and Western Turkey, constantly watching which was rising and attaching or rebelling without fixed loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between Eastern and Western Turkey, the three clans watched which power was ascendant and shifted allegiance without constancy.

sentences.zh: 後稍南徙，自號「三姓葉護」，兵強，甘於鬥，廷州以西諸突厥皆畏之。

translations.literal: They later drifted somewhat south, styled themselves the "Three-Surname Yabghu," grew strong in arms, loved battle, and all Turkish peoples west of Tingzhou feared them.
translations.idiomatic: They gradually moved south, took the title "Three-Surname Yabghu," grew formidable in war, delighted in fighting, and every Turkish group west of Tingzhou stood in awe of them.

sentences.zh: 開元初，再來朝。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era they came to court twice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan they presented themselves at court on two occasions.

sentences.zh: 天寶時，與回紇、拔悉蜜共攻殺烏蘇米施可汗，又與回紇擊拔悉蜜，走其可汗阿史那施於北庭，奔京師。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era they joined the Huihe and Basmil in killing Qaghan Wusumishi, then with the Huihe attacked the Basmil, driving their qaghan Ashna Shi to Beiting, whence he fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao they allied with the Huihe and Basmil to kill Qaghan Wusumishi, then with the Huihe struck the Basmil and drove qaghan Ashna Shi to Beiting and on to the capital.

sentences.zh: 葛祿與九姓復立回紇葉護，所謂懷仁可汗者也。

translations.literal: The Geluolu and the Nine Surnames then set up the Huihe yabghu—the so-called Qutluq qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Geluolu and the Nine Surnames thereupon enthroned a Huihe yabghu—the Qutluq qaghan of tradition.

sentences.zh: 於是葛祿之處烏德犍山者臣回紇，在金山、北庭者自立葉護，歲來朝。

translations.literal: The Geluolu on Wudejian Mountain then submitted to the Huihe; those at the Altai and Beiting set up their own yabghu and came to court yearly.
translations.idiomatic: The Geluolu on Wudejian Mountain submitted to the Huihe, while those at the Altai and Beiting maintained an independent yabghu and paid yearly court visits.

sentences.zh: 久之，葉護頓毗伽縛突厥叛酋阿布思，進封金山郡王。

translations.literal: After a time Yabghu Dund pijia bound the Turkish rebel chief Abu Si and was advanced to Prince of Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In time Yabghu Dund pijia captured the Turkish rebel chief Abu Si and was enfeoffed Prince of Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 天寶間，凡五朝。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao period they came to court five times in all.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tianbao reign they presented themselves at court five times altogether.

sentences.zh: 至德後，葛邏祿浸盛，與回紇爭強，徙十姓可汗故地，盡有碎葉、怛邏斯諸城。

translations.literal: After the Zhide era the Geluolu grew ever stronger, vied with the Huihe for dominance, moved into the old lands of the Ten Surnames qaghan, and held all the cities from Suyab to Talas.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide the Geluolu waxed powerful, contested supremacy with the Huihe, shifted into the former domains of the Ten Surnames qaghan, and held Suyab, Talas, and the cities between.

sentences.zh: 然限回紇，故朝會不能自達於朝。

translations.literal: Yet hemmed in by the Huihe, they could not present themselves at court except through them.
translations.idiomatic: Still checked by the Huihe, they could not reach the court on their own and had to come only through Huihe channels.

sentences.zh: 拔悉蜜，貞觀二十三年始來朝。

translations.literal: The Basmil first came to court in the twenty-third year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: The Basmil first presented themselves at court in Zhenguan 23.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，與回紇葉護擊殺突厥可汗，立拔悉蜜大酋阿史那施為賀臘毗伽可汗，遣使者入謝，玄宗賜紫文袍、金鈿帶、魚袋。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era, together with the Huihe yabghu they killed the Turkish qaghan, set up the Basmil grand chief Ashna Shi as Helapijia qaghan, and sent envoys to give thanks; Xuanzong granted him a purple patterned robe, gold-inlaid belt, and fish pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao, allied with the Huihe yabghu, they slew the Turkish qaghan and enthroned the Basmil grand chief Ashna Shi as Helapijia qaghan. His envoys came to give thanks, and Xuanzong bestowed a purple patterned robe, gold-inlaid belt, and fish tally pouch.

sentences.zh: 不三歲，為葛邏祿、回紇所破，奔北庭。

translations.literal: Within less than three years they were broken by the Geluolu and Huihe and fled to Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: In less than three years the Geluolu and Huihe shattered them, and they fled to Beiting.

sentences.zh: 後朝京師，拜左武衛將軍，地與眾歸回紇。

translations.literal: Later he came to the capital and was appointed Left Martial Guard general; his territory and people were returned to the Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: He later presented himself at court and was made Left Martial Guard general, while his lands and followers were turned over to the Huihe.

sentences.zh: 都播，亦曰都波，其地北瀕小海，西堅昆，南回紇，分三部，皆自統制。

translations.literal: The Dubo were also called Dubo; their land bordered the lesser sea on the north, Jiegu on the west, and the Huihe on the south, divided into three parts, each under its own rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Dubo—also Dubo—lay north against the lesser sea, west against the Kirghiz, south against the Huihe, and were split into three divisions, each self-governing.

sentences.zh: 其俗無歲時。

translations.literal: Their custom had no seasonal calendar.
translations.idiomatic: They kept no seasonal calendar.

sentences.zh: 結草為廬。

translations.literal: They bound grass into huts.
translations.idiomatic: They wove grass into shelters.

sentences.zh: 無畜牧，不知稼穡，土多百合草，掇其根以飯，捕魚、鳥、獸食之。

translations.literal: They had no livestock and knew nothing of planting; the land abounded in lily roots, which they dug for food, and they ate fish, birds, and beasts they caught.
translations.idiomatic: Without herds or fields, they lived on lily roots dug from soil thick with lilies, supplementing their diet with fish, fowl, and game.

sentences.zh: 衣貂鹿皮，貧者緝鳥羽為服。

translations.literal: They wore sable and deer skins; the poor stitched bird feathers into garments.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy dressed in sable and deerskin; the poor pieced garments from bird feathers.

sentences.zh: 其昏姻，富者納馬，貧者效鹿皮草根。

translations.literal: In marriage the rich paid horses as bride-price; the poor offered deer hides and grass roots instead.
translations.idiomatic: For marriage the rich paid horses; the poor substituted deer hides and grass roots.

sentences.zh: 死以木櫝斂置山中，或系於樹，送葬哭泣，與突厥同。

translations.literal: The dead were enclosed in wooden coffins and placed in the mountains, or hung from trees; funeral weeping followed the Turkish custom.
translations.idiomatic: They coffined the dead in wood and set them in the hills or hung them in trees, mourning at burial as the Turks did.

sentences.zh: 無刑罰，盜者倍輸其贓。

translations.literal: There was no criminal punishment; thieves paid double the stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: They had no penal code; thieves made restitution at double value.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十一年，因骨利幹入朝，亦以使通中國。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, entering court through the Guligan, they also sent envoys to communicate with China.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 21 they came to court by way of the Guligan and thereafter maintained contact through envoys.

sentences.zh: 骨利幹處瀚海北，勝兵五千。

translations.literal: The Guligan lay north of the Hanhai; fit warriors numbered five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Guligan lived north of the Hanhai with five thousand men under arms.

sentences.zh: 草多百合。

translations.literal: Grass grew abundantly with lilies.
translations.idiomatic: Lilies grew thickly across their pastures.

sentences.zh: 產良馬，首似橐它，筋骼壯大，日中馳數百里。

translations.literal: They produced fine horses whose heads resembled camels, sinews and bones powerful, running several hundred li at midday.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses were superb: heads like camels, frames powerful enough to gallop hundreds of li in the heat of noon.

sentences.zh: 其地北距海，去京師最遠，又北度海則晝長夜短，日入亨羊胛，熟，東方已明，蓋近日出處也。

translations.literal: Their land reached the northern sea and lay farthest from the capital; crossing the sea northward, day was long and night short—at sunset a lamb's shoulder would cook through, and the east was already bright, for they were near where the sun rises.
translations.idiomatic: North to the sea and farther from the capital than any tributary, their country lay so near the sunrise that beyond the northern waters days ran long: a lamb's shoulder could cook from sundown before the eastern sky had fully darkened.

sentences.zh: 既入朝，詔遣雲麾將軍康蘇蜜勞答，以其地為玄闕州。

translations.literal: After they entered court, Cloud-Banner general Kang Sumi was sent to comfort and reply; their land was made Xuanque prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had presented themselves, Cloud-Banner general Kang Sumi was dispatched to receive them, and their territory was organized as Xuanque prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其大酋俟斤因使者獻馬，帝取其異者號十驥，皆為美名：曰「騰霜白」，曰「皎雪驄』，曰「凝露驄」，曰「縣光驄」，曰「決波騟』，曰「飛霞驃」，曰「發電赤」，曰「流金瓜」，曰「翔麟紫」，曰「奔虹赤」，厚禮其使。

translations.literal: The grand irkin presented horses through the envoy; the Emperor chose the most remarkable and named ten steeds, each with a fine title: "Soaring Frost White," "Gleaming Snow Piebald," "Condensed Dew Piebald," "Suspended Light Piebald," "Breaking Wave Piebald," "Flying Rosy Cloud Piebald," "Lightning Red," "Flowing Gold Melon," "Soaring Unicorn Purple," and "Galloping Rainbow Red," and richly rewarded the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Through his envoy the grand irkin offered horses; the emperor selected ten exceptional mounts and gave each a ceremonial name—Soaring Frost White, Gleaming Snow Piebald, Condensed Dew Piebald, Suspended Light Piebald, Breaking Wave Piebald, Flying Rosy Cloud Piebald, Lightning Red, Flowing Gold Melon, Soaring Unicorn Purple, and Galloping Rainbow Red—and lavished gifts on the embassy.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，以玄闕州更為余吾州，隸瀚海都督府。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo era Xuanque prefecture was renamed Yuwu prefecture and placed under the Hanhai Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo, Xuanque was renamed Yuwu and subordinated to the Hanhai Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 延載初，亦來朝。

translations.literal: In the early Yanzai period they again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanzai reign they returned to court.

sentences.zh: 白霫居鮮卑故地，直京師東北五千里，與同羅、仆骨接。

translations.literal: The Baixi occupied the old Xianbei lands, five thousand li northeast of the capital, adjoining the Tongluo and Pugu.
translations.idiomatic: The Baixi held the former Xianbei country, five thousand li northeast of the capital, bordering the Tongluo and Pugu.

sentences.zh: 避薛延陀，保奧支水、冷陘山，南契丹，北烏羅渾，東靺鞨，西拔野古，地圓袤二千里，山繚其外，勝兵萬人。

translations.literal: Fleeing the Xueyantuo they held the Aozhi River and Lengling Mountains, with the Khitan to the south, Wuluohun to the north, Mohe to the east, and Bayegu to the west—a domain two thousand li round, ringed by mountains, with ten thousand effectives.
translations.idiomatic: Driven from the Xueyantuo they sheltered on the Aozhi River and Lengling range: Khitan south, Wuluohun north, Mohe east, Bayegu west. Their land ran two thousand li in circuit, mountains hemming it in, with ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 業射獵，以赤皮緣衣，婦貫銅釧，以子鈴綴襟。

translations.literal: They lived by hunting and archery, edged garments with red trim, and women wore copper bracelets with small bells sewn to the collar.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting and the bow were their livelihood. Men trimmed clothing with red borders; women wore copper bracelets and bells at the throat.

sentences.zh: 其部有三：曰居延，曰無若沒，曰潢水。

translations.literal: The tribe had three divisions: Juyan, Wuruomo, and Huangshui.
translations.idiomatic: Three branches made up the people: Juyan, Wuruomo, and Huangshui.

sentences.zh: 其君長臣突厥頡利可汗為俟斤。

translations.literal: Their chieftain served Turkish qaghan Jieli as irkin.
translations.idiomatic: Their ruler had served Turkish qaghan Jieli as irkin.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中再來朝，後列其地為寘顏州，以別部為居延州，即用俟斤為刺史。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan they came to court twice; later their land was listed as Zhenyan prefecture and a separate division as Juyan prefecture, the irkin himself made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: They presented themselves twice in Zhenguan; afterward their territory became Zhenyan prefecture, with a separate Juyan prefecture, and the irkin was made prefect.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，授酋長李含珠為居延都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing, tribal chief Li Hanzhu was appointed Juyan protector.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 5 chief Li Hanzhu was named Juyan protector.

sentences.zh: 含珠死，弟厥都繼之。

translations.literal: When Hanzhu died, his younger brother Juedu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhu died; his brother Juedu followed.

sentences.zh: 後無聞焉。

translations.literal: Afterward nothing more is heard of them.
translations.idiomatic: No further record of them survives.

sentences.zh: 斛薛處多濫葛北，勝兵萬人。

translations.literal: The Huxue lay north of the Duolange with ten thousand effectives.
translations.idiomatic: The Huxue lived north of the Duolange with ten thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 奚結處同羅北，思結在延陀故牙，二部合兵凡二萬。

translations.literal: The Xijie lay north of the Tongluo; the Sijie at the Xueyantuo's old royal camp—the two tribes together fielded twenty thousand troops.
