translations.idiomatic: The Xijie were north of the Tongluo; the Sijie at the Xueyantuo's former headquarters. Together they could muster twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 既來朝，列其地州縣之。

translations.literal: Once they came to court, their lands were organized into prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: After presenting themselves at court, their territories were carved into prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，北狄能自通者，又有烏羅渾，或曰烏洛侯，曰烏羅護，直京師東北六千里而贏，東靺鞨，西突厥，南契丹，北烏丸，大抵風俗皆靺鞨也。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time among the northern Di who could reach the court on their own were also the Wuluohun, also called Wuluohou or Wuluhu, six thousand li northeast of the capital by the longer route: Mohe east, Turks west, Khitan south, Wuhuan north—their ways were largely those of the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong other northern peoples who opened their own relations included the Wuluohun—also Wuluohou or Wuluhu—six thousand li northeast by the circuitous road: Mohe east, Turks west, Khitan south, Wuhuan north. In custom they were much like the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 烏丸或曰古丸。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan were also called Guwan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan were also known as Guwan.

sentences.zh: 又有鞠，或曰祴，居拔野古東北，有木無草，地多苔。

translations.literal: There were also the Ju, or Kai, northeast of the Bayegu, with trees but no grass and ground thick with moss.
translations.idiomatic: Farther northeast of the Bayegu lived the Ju—also Kai—where trees grew but grass did not and moss carpeted the earth.

sentences.zh: 無羊馬，人豢鹿若牛馬，惟食苔，俗以駕車。

translations.literal: They had no sheep or horses; people raised deer like cattle, fed them only moss, and used them to draw carts.
translations.idiomatic: Without sheep or horses they kept deer as others keep cattle, fed them moss alone, and harnessed them to carts.

sentences.zh: 又以鹿皮為衣，聚木作屋，尊卑共居。

translations.literal: They made clothing of deerskin and built communal wooden houses where high and low dwelt together.
translations.idiomatic: Deerskin served for dress; timber houses housed nobles and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 又有俞折者，地差大，俗與拔野古相埒。

translations.literal: There were also the Yuzhe, a somewhat larger territory whose customs rivaled those of the Bayegu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuzhe held a somewhat larger domain with customs much like the Bayegu's.

sentences.zh: 少羊馬，多貂鼠。

translations.literal: They had few sheep and horses but many sables and martens.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horses were scarce; sables and martens abundant.

sentences.zh: 又有駁馬者，或曰弊剌，曰遏羅支，直突厥之北，距京師萬四千里。

translations.literal: There were also the Boma, or Bila, or Eluozhi, directly north of the Turks, fourteen thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Turks lived the Boma—also Bila or Eluozhi—fourteen thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 隨水草，然喜居山，勝兵三萬。

translations.literal: They followed pasture and water yet preferred mountain dwelling; effectives numbered thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture and water guided their movements, yet they favored the high country, with thirty thousand men under arms.

sentences.zh: 地常積雪，木不雕。

translations.literal: Snow lay deep year-round; trees did not rot.
translations.idiomatic: Snow never left the ground; timber did not decay.

sentences.zh: 以馬耕田，馬色皆駁，因以名國雲。

translations.literal: They plowed with horses, all piebald in color, and so named their state.
translations.idiomatic: They farmed with horses—all piebald—and took that as their country's name.

sentences.zh: 北極於海，雖畜馬而不乘，資湩酪以食。

translations.literal: Their northern limit was the sea; though they kept horses they did not ride them, living on mare's milk and curds.
translations.idiomatic: North to the sea they raised horses but did not ride, sustaining themselves on kumiss and curds.

sentences.zh: 好與結骨戰，人貌多似結骨，而語不相通。

translations.literal: They loved fighting the Jiegu; their appearance resembled the Jiegu, yet their speech did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: They warred constantly with the Jiegu, looked much like them, yet spoke a different tongue.

sentences.zh: 皆劗發，樺皮帽。

translations.literal: All shaved the head and wore birch-bark caps.
translations.idiomatic: Men cropped their hair and wore birch-bark hats.

sentences.zh: 構木類井幹，覆樺為室。

translations.literal: They built timber frames like well-curbs and roofed them with birch bark.
translations.idiomatic: Houses rose on timber frames like well-shafts, roofed in birch bark.

sentences.zh: 各有小君長，不能相臣也。

translations.literal: Each had a petty chieftain and none could rule the others.
translations.idiomatic: Petty chiefs ruled separate bands; none could command the rest.

sentences.zh: 大漢者，處鞠之北，饒羊馬，人物頎大，故以自名。

translations.literal: The Dahan lay north of the Ju, rich in sheep and horses; their people were tall and sturdy, and they took that as their name.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Ju were the Dahan, plentiful in sheep and horses, tall of stature—"Great Han" was the name they gave themselves.

sentences.zh: 與鞠俱鄰於黠戛斯劍海之瀕。

translations.literal: Both bordered the Kirghiz Sword Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Both neighbored the Kirghiz on the Sword Sea.

sentences.zh: 此皆古所未賓者，當貞觀逮永徽，奉貂馬入朝，或一再至。

translations.literal: None of these had submitted in antiquity; from Zhenguan through Yonghui they presented sable and horses at court, some once, some twice.
translations.idiomatic: None had bowed to earlier dynasties; between Zhenguan and Yonghui they began sending sable and horses—some once, some repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯，古堅昆國也。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz were the ancient state of Jiegu.
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz were the old realm of Jiegu.

sentences.zh: 地當伊吾之西，焉耆北，白山之旁。

translations.literal: Their land lay west of Yiwu, north of Kucha, beside White Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They held the country west of Yiwu, north of Kucha, along White Mountain.

sentences.zh: 或曰居勿，曰結骨。

translations.literal: They were also called Juwu, or Jiegu.
translations.idiomatic: They were also known as Juwu or Jiegu.

sentences.zh: 其種雜丁零，乃匈奴西鄙也。

translations.literal: Their stock mingled with the Dingling; they were the western marches of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Their people mingled Dingling blood—they were the Xiongnu's western fringe.

sentences.zh: 匈奴封漢降將李陵為右賢王，衛律為丁零王。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu enfeoffed the Han defector Li Ling as Right Worthy King and Wei Lü as King of the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu had made the Han turncoat Li Ling Right Worthy King and Wei Lü king of the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 後郅支單於破堅昆，於時東距單於廷七千里，南車師五千里，郅支留都之。

translations.literal: Later Qaghan Zhizhi destroyed Jiegu; at that time it lay seven thousand li east of the qaghan's court and five thousand li south of the Chief of the Chariots; Zhizhi made it his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qaghan Zhizhi overthrew Jiegu when it stood seven thousand li east of his court and five thousand li south of the Chief of the Chariots; Zhizhi then kept his seat there.

sentences.zh: 故後世得其地者訛為結骨，稍號紇骨，亦曰紇扢斯雲。

translations.literal: Hence later holders of the land corrupted the name to Jiegu, then gradually Gegu, also written Hegesi.
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers corrupted the name to Jiegu, then Gegu, also Hegesi.

sentences.zh: 眾數十萬，勝兵八萬，直回紇西北三千里，南依貪漫山。

translations.literal: Their numbers reached several hundred thousand; effectives eighty thousand; they lay three thousand li northwest of the Huihe, south against Tanhan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They numbered in the hundreds of thousands with eighty thousand warriors, three thousand li northwest of the Huihe, south along Tanhan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 地夏沮洳，冬積雪。

translations.literal: In summer the ground was damp; in winter snow accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Summers were sodden; winters buried in snow.

sentences.zh: 人皆長大，赤發、皙面、綠瞳，以黑髮為不祥。

translations.literal: The people were tall, with red hair, fair faces, and green eyes; black hair was considered ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: They were tall, red-haired, fair-skinned, green-eyed; black hair was deemed unlucky.

sentences.zh: 黑瞳者，必曰陵苗裔也。

translations.literal: Those with black pupils were sure to be called descendants of Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone with black pupils was declared a descendant of Li Ling.

sentences.zh: 男少女多，以環貫耳，俗趫伉，男子有男黥其手，女已嫁黥項。

translations.literal: Men outnumbered women; they wore rings in the ears; the people were vigorous. Men tattooed the hand when a son was born; married women tattooed the neck.
translations.idiomatic: Men were more numerous than women, wore ear-rings, and were fierce by nature. Fathers tattooed the hand at a son's birth; married women tattooed the neck.

sentences.zh: 雜居多淫佚。

translations.literal: Mixed dwelling led to much license.
translations.idiomatic: Communal living bred widespread looseness of morals.

sentences.zh: 謂歲首為茂師哀，以三哀為一時，以十二物紀年，如歲在寅則曰虎年。

translations.literal: They called the year-opening Maoshi'ai; three Maoshi made a season; twelve creatures marked the years—as in a year of yin they said the Year of the Tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Their new year was Maoshi'ai; three Maoshi formed a season; twelve animal signs marked the years, as "Tiger Year" for a yin year.

sentences.zh: 氣多寒，雖大河亦半冰。

translations.literal: The air was mostly cold; even great rivers were half frozen.
translations.idiomatic: Cold dominated the climate; even major rivers froze halfway across.

sentences.zh: 稼有禾、粟、大小麥、青稞，步硙以為面糜。

translations.literal: They planted millet, grain, wheat large and small, and highland barley, treading millstones to make flour porridge.
translations.idiomatic: Crops included millet, grain, large and small wheat, and highland barley, ground on foot mills into porridge flour.

sentences.zh: 穄以三月種，九月獲，以飯，以釀酒，而無果蔬。

translations.literal: Broomcorn millet was sown in the third month and harvested in the ninth, eaten as grain or brewed into wine; fruits and vegetables they had none.
translations.idiomatic: Broomcorn millet went in the ground in the third month and came off in the ninth, eaten as food or fermented into wine; they grew no fruit or vegetables.

sentences.zh: 畜，馬至壯大，以善鬥者為頭馬，有橐它、牛、羊，牛為多，富農至數千。

translations.literal: Livestock: horses grew very large; the best fighters were made lead horses. They had camels, cattle, and sheep—cattle most numerous; wealthy farmers might own thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Horses grew to great size; the fiercest in battle led the herd. Camels, cattle, and sheep were kept—cattle most of all; a rich man might own thousands.

sentences.zh: 其獸有野馬、骨咄、黃羊、原羝、鹿、黑尾，黑尾者似獐，尾大而黑。

translations.literal: Wild beasts included wild horses, gudu, yellow sheep, plain antelope, deer, and black-tail—the black-tail resembling the roe deer with large black tail.
translations.idiomatic: Game included wild horses, gudu, yellow sheep, plain antelope, deer, and black-tail, the last like a roe deer with a large black tail.

sentences.zh: 魚，有蔑者長七八尺，莫痕者無骨，口出頤下。

translations.literal: Fish: the mie was seven or eight chi long; the mohen had no bones, the mouth protruding below the jaw.
translations.idiomatic: Among fish, the mie reached seven or eight chi; the mohen was boneless, its mouth thrusting forward beneath the jaw.

sentences.zh: 鳥，雁、鶩、烏鵲、鷹、隼。

translations.literal: Birds: wild geese, ducks, magpies, hawks, and falcons.
translations.idiomatic: Birds included wild geese, ducks, magpies, hawks, and falcons.

sentences.zh: 木，松、樺、榆、柳、蒲。

translations.literal: Trees: pine, birch, elm, willow, and bulrush.
translations.idiomatic: Timber included pine, birch, elm, willow, and bulrush.

sentences.zh: 松高者仰射不能及顛，而樺尤多。

translations.literal: Tall pines could not be topped by an upward shot; birch was especially abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Pines grew so high an arrow shot upward could not reach the crown; birch was everywhere.

sentences.zh: 有金、鐵、錫，每雨，俗必得鐵，號迦沙，為兵絕犀利，常以輸突厥。

translations.literal: They had gold, iron, and tin; after rain the people were sure to find iron they called jasha, weapons of surpassing sharpness, often supplied to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, iron, and tin lay in their hills; after rain they gathered iron called jasha, forged into blades of exceptional edge, much of it sent to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 其戰有弓矢、旗幟，其騎士析木為盾，蔽股足，又以圓盾傅肩，而捍矢刃。

translations.literal: In war they used bow, arrow, and banners; horsemen split wood for shields covering thigh and foot, and round shields on the shoulder to ward off blades.
translations.idiomatic: They fought with bow, arrow, and standards; cavalry split planks into shields for thighs and feet and wore round shoulder shields against edged weapons.

sentences.zh: 其君曰「阿熱」，遂姓阿熱氏，建一纛，下皆尚赤，余以部落為之號。

translations.literal: Their ruler was called "A-re," and the surname A-re was established; one great banner was raised, all below honoring red; the rest took tribal names.
translations.idiomatic: Their king was titled A-re, from which came the royal A-re clan; a great banner stood above a realm that favored red, while lesser tribes kept their own names.

sentences.zh: 服貴貂、豽，阿熱冬帽貂，夏帽金扣，銳頂而卷末，諸下皆帽白氈，喜佩刀礪，賤者衣皮不帽，女衣毳毼、錦、罽、綾，蓋安西、北庭、大食所貿售也。

translations.literal: They prized sable and badger fur; A-re's winter cap was sable, summer cap gold-clasped, pointed and curled at the tip; subordinates wore white felt caps, loved girded swords and whetstones; the poor wore skins without caps. Women wore wool, brocade, felt, and silk traded from Anxi, Beiting, and Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: Rank showed in sable and badger dress: the A-re wore sable in winter, a gold-clasped peaked summer cap with curled tip; followers wore white felt and belted blades. The poor went bareheaded in hides. Women dressed in wool, brocade, felt, and silk from Anxi, Beiting, and the Arab lands.

sentences.zh: 阿熱駐牙青山，周柵代垣，聯氈為帳，號「密的支」，它首領居小帳。

translations.literal: A-re's headquarters stood at Green Mountain, palisades replacing walls, felt tents joined called "Midezhi"; other chiefs dwelt in lesser tents.
translations.idiomatic: The A-re encamped on Green Mountain behind stockades, his great felt hall called Midezhi while lesser chiefs kept smaller tents.

sentences.zh: 凡調兵，諸部役屬者悉行。

translations.literal: Whenever troops were mobilized, all subordinate tribes must march.
translations.idiomatic: At mobilization every dependent tribe was called to the field.

sentences.zh: 內貂鼠、青鼠為賦。

translations.literal: Tribute inland was sable and blue rat furs.
translations.idiomatic: They paid tribute in sable and blue rat pelts.

sentences.zh: 其官，宰相、都督、職使、長史、將軍、達幹六等。

translations.literal: Their offices were six ranks: chancellor, protector, duty commissioner, chief secretary, general, and taghan.
translations.idiomatic: Six grades of office existed: chancellor, protector, duty commissioner, chief secretary, general, and taghan.

sentences.zh: 宰相七，都督三、職使十，皆典兵；

translations.literal: Seven chancellors, three protectors, and ten duty commissioners—all commanded troops;
translations.idiomatic: Seven chancellors, three protectors, and ten duty commissioners held military authority;

sentences.zh: 長史十五，將軍、達幹無員。

translations.literal: fifteen chief secretaries; generals and taghans without fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: fifteen chief secretaries; generals and taghans without fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 諸部食肉及馬酪，惟阿熱設餅餌。

translations.literal: All tribes ate meat and mare's milk; only the A-re was served bread and cakes.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes lived on meat and kumiss; only the A-re received bread and pastry.

sentences.zh: 樂有笛、鼓、笙、觱篥、盤鈴。

translations.literal: Music had flute, drum, sheng, bili, and hand-bells.
translations.idiomatic: Their music used flute, drum, sheng, bili pipe, and hand-bells.

sentences.zh: 戲有弄駝、師子、馬伎、繩伎。

translations.literal: Entertainments included camel tricks, lion play, horsemanship, and rope dancing.
translations.idiomatic: Games featured camel performance, lion dance, horsemanship, and rope acrobatics.

sentences.zh: 祠神惟主水草，祭無時，呼巫為「甘」。

translations.literal: They worshipped water and grass without fixed seasons; shamans were called "Gan."
translations.idiomatic: Their gods were water and pasture, worshipped without calendar; shamans were called Gan.

sentences.zh: 昏嫁納羊馬以聘，富者或百千計。

translations.literal: Marriage bride-price was paid in sheep and horses; the rich might give a hundred or a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage required sheep and horses; the wealthy paid hundreds or thousands.

sentences.zh: 喪不剺面，三環屍哭，乃火之，收其骨，歲而乃墓，然後器泣有節。

translations.literal: At death they did not lacerate the face; mourners circled the corpse thrice weeping, then burned it and gathered the bones; after a year they buried them, and only then did ritual weeping observe proper limits.
translations.idiomatic: They did not scar their faces for the dead. Kin circled the body wailing three times, burned it, collected the bones, buried them after a year, and only then observed measured mourning.

sentences.zh: 冬處室，木皮為覆。

translations.literal: In winter they dwelt indoors with birch bark for roofing.
translations.idiomatic: Winter quarters were roofed in birch bark.

sentences.zh: 其文字言語，與回鶻正同。

translations.literal: Their script and speech were identical with the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Writing and language matched those of the Uyghurs exactly.

sentences.zh: 法最嚴，臨陣橈、奉使不稱、妄議國若盜者皆斷首；

translations.literal: Their law was the strictest: cowardice in battle, failure of an envoy's charge, or reckless talk about the state, like theft, meant beheading;
translations.idiomatic: Law was severe: flinching in battle, an envoy's dereliction, or loose talk about the realm, like theft, brought decapitation;

sentences.zh: 子為盜，以首著父頸，非死不脫。

translations.literal: if a son stole, his head was hung on the father's neck and not removed until the father died.
translations.idiomatic: a son's theft meant his head was hung at the father's neck until the father died.

sentences.zh: 阿熱牙至回鶻牙所，橐它四十日行。

translations.literal: From the A-re's camp to the Uyghur royal camp was forty days by camel.
translations.idiomatic: Forty camel-days lay between the A-re's headquarters and the Uyghur royal camp.

sentences.zh: 使者道出天德右二百里許抵西受降城，北三百里許至鵜泉，泉西北至回鶻牙千五百里許，而有東、西二道，泉之北，東道也。

translations.literal: Envoys' route left Tiande about two hundred li west to West Shouxiang city, then north about three hundred li to Piquan; northwest from the spring to the Uyghur camp was about fifteen hundred li, with eastern and western roads—the northern road east of the spring.
translations.idiomatic: The embassy road ran two hundred li west from Tiande to West Shouxiang city, three hundred li north to Piquan, then some fifteen hundred li northwest to the Uyghur court by eastern or western routes—the eastern road lying north of the spring.

sentences.zh: 回鶻牙北六百里得仙娥河，河東北曰雪山，地多水泉。

translations.literal: Six hundred li north of the Uyghur camp was the Xian'e River; northeast of the river lay Snow Mountain, a land of many springs.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred li north of the Uyghur camp stood the Xian'e River; northeast rose Snow Mountain, rich in springs.

sentences.zh: 青山之東，有水曰劍河，偶艇以度，水悉東北流，經其國，合而北入於海。

translations.literal: East of Green Mountain a stream called the Sword River was crossed by raft; its waters all flowed northeast through their country, joined, and entered the sea northward.
translations.idiomatic: East of Green Mountain the Sword River was crossed on rafts; its waters ran northeast through their land, united, and poured north into the sea.

sentences.zh: 東至木馬突厥三部落，曰都播、彌列、哥餓支，其酋長皆為頡斤。

translations.literal: East to the three tribes of Wooden-Horse Turkey—Dubo, Milie, and Ge'ezh—whose chiefs were all irkin.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward lay three Wooden-Horse Turkish tribes—Dubo, Milie, and Ge'ezh—each ruled by an irkin.

sentences.zh: 樺皮覆室，多善馬，俗乘木馬馳冰上，以板藉足，屈木支腋，蹴輒百步，勢迅激。

translations.literal: Birch bark roofed their dwellings; horses were plentiful; custom favored wooden sledges on ice, boards bound to the feet, bent wood braced under the arm—one kick carried a hundred paces with violent speed.
translations.idiomatic: They roofed in birch, bred fine horses, and on ice rode wooden runners: boards on the feet, bent poles under the arms—one push sent them a hundred paces at furious speed.

sentences.zh: 夜鈔盜，晝伏匿，堅昆之人得以役屬之。

translations.literal: They plundered by night and hid by day; the Kirghiz could make them serve.
translations.idiomatic: They raided at night and hid by day, and the Kirghiz could reduce them to servitude.

sentences.zh: 堅昆，本強國也，地與突厥等，突厥以女妻其酋豪，東至骨利幹，南吐蕃，西南葛邏祿。

translations.literal: Jiegu was originally a powerful state; its territory equaled that of the Turks, who gave their daughters in marriage to its chiefs. East to the Guligan, south to Tibet, southwest to the Geluolu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiegu had been a great power, its lands the equal of the Turks', who married their daughters to its chiefs. It reached east to the Guligan, south to Tibet, and southwest to the Geluolu.

sentences.zh: 始隸薛延陀，延陀以頡利發一人監國。

translations.literal: At first it submitted to the Xueyantuo; the Xueyantuo sent one jielifa to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: It first bowed to the Xueyantuo, who posted a single jielifa to supervise the realm.

sentences.zh: 其酋長三人，曰訖悉輩，曰居沙波輩，曰阿米輩，共治其國，未始與中國通。

translations.literal: Its chiefs were three: Qixibei, Jushabobei, and Amibei, who jointly ruled the state and had never communicated with China.
translations.idiomatic: Three chiefs—Qixibei, Jushabobei, and Amibei—governed together and had never opened relations with China.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十二年，聞鐵勒等已入臣，即遣使者獻方物，其酋長俟利發失缽屈阿棧身入朝，太宗勞享之，謂群臣曰：「往渭橋斬三突厥，自謂功多，今俟利發在席，更覺過之。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan, hearing that the Tiele and others had already submitted, they immediately sent envoys with local products; Irkin Shiboju A-zhan came in person. Taizong feasted and comforted him, telling his ministers: "When I beheaded three Turks at Wei Bridge I thought my merit great; now with Irkin in attendance I feel I have surpassed myself.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 22, learning that the Tiele and others had submitted, they sent tribute at once. Irkin Shiboju A-zhan came in person; Taizong feasted him and told the court: "When I slew three Turks at Wei Bridge I thought my achievement unmatched—yet with this irkin at my table I find I have outdone myself.

sentences.zh: 俟利發酒酣，奏願得持笏，帝以其地為堅昆府，拜俟利發左屯衛大將軍，即為都督，隸燕然都護。

translations.literal: When Irkin was deep in wine he asked to hold the court tablet; the Emperor made his land the Jiegu Protectorate, appointed Irkin Left Garrison Guard grand general and protector, subordinate to the Yanran Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: Wine warmed, the irkin begged to hold a court tablet. The emperor organized his territory as the Jiegu Protectorate, named him Left Garrison Guard grand general and protector under the Yanran Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 高宗世，再來朝。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's reign they came to court twice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong they presented themselves twice.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，獻方物，中宗引使者勞之曰：「而國與我同宗，非它蕃比。」

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era they offered local products; Zhongzong received the envoys and comforted them: "Your state shares our clan—it is not like other barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong they sent tribute; Zhongzong received the embassy and said: "Your country and ours are of one clan—not to be compared with other foreign peoples.

sentences.zh: 屬以酒，使者頓首。

translations.literal: He bestowed wine; the envoy bowed to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offered wine; the envoy kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 玄宗世，四朝獻。

translations.literal: In Xuanzong's time they presented tribute four times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanzong they came to court four times.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，為回紇所破，自是不能通中國。

translations.literal: In the Qianyuan era they were broken by the Huihe and thereafter could no longer reach China.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan the Huihe shattered them, and thereafter they could not communicate with the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 後狄語訛為黠戛斯，蓋回鶻謂之，若曰黃赤面雲，又訛為戛戛斯。

translations.literal: Later the barbarian tongue corrupted the name to Kirghiz, as the Uyghurs called them—something like "yellow-red faces"—and it was further corrupted to Gagas.
translations.idiomatic: Di speech later slurred the name into Kirghiz—the Uyghur term, roughly "yellow-red faces"—and still further into Gagas.

sentences.zh: 然常與大食、吐蕃、葛祿相依杖，吐蕃之往來者畏回鶻剽鈔，必住葛祿，以待黠戛斯護送。

translations.literal: Yet they constantly relied on the Arabs, Tibet, and Geluolu; Tibetans traveling back and forth feared Uyghur raiders and had to lodge with the Geluolu, waiting for Kirghiz escort.
translations.idiomatic: They leaned on the Arabs, Tibet, and Geluolu alike. Tibetan travelers, fearing Uyghur raids, lodged with the Geluolu until Kirghiz escorts could see them through.

sentences.zh: 大食有重錦，其載二十橐它乃勝，既不可兼負，故裁為二十匹，每三歲一餉黠戛斯。

translations.literal: The Arabs had heavy brocade that twenty camels were needed to carry; it could not be borne at once, so it was cut into twenty bolts, presented to the Kirghiz every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Arab heavy brocade required twenty camels per load; since it could not be carried whole, it was cut into twenty bolts and sent to the Kirghiz every three years.

sentences.zh: 而回鶻授其君長阿熱官為「毗伽頓頡斤」。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs invested their ruler A-re with the title "Pijia Dund Irkin."
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs gave their ruler A-re the title Pijia Dund Irkin.

sentences.zh: 回鶻稍衰，阿熱即自稱可汗。

translations.literal: As the Uyghurs gradually weakened, A-re styled himself qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs waned, A-re proclaimed himself qaghan.

sentences.zh: 其母，突騎施女也，為母可敦；

translations.literal: His mother was a Turgesh woman and was made Mother Qatun;
translations.idiomatic: His mother, a Turgesh woman, was styled Mother Qatun;

sentences.zh: 妻葛祿葉護女，為可敦。

translations.literal: his wife was a Geluolu yabghu's daughter and was made Qatun.
translations.idiomatic: his wife, daughter of a Geluolu yabghu, was made Qatun.

sentences.zh: 回鶻遣宰相伐之，不勝，挐鬥二十年不解。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs sent a chancellor to attack him but could not win; grappling continued twenty years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs sent a chancellor against him and failed; the two sides grappled twenty years without end.

sentences.zh: 阿熱恃勝，乃肆詈曰：「爾運盡矣！

translations.literal: Relying on victory, A-re then reviled them openly: "Your fortune is spent!
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by success, A-re hurled insults: "Your luck is finished!

sentences.zh: 我將收爾金帳，於爾帳前馳我馬，植我旗，爾能抗，亟來，即不能，當疾去。」

translations.literal: I will take your golden tent; before your tent I will ride my horse and plant my banner—if you can resist, come at once; if not, leave quickly.
translations.idiomatic: I will seize your golden tent, ride my horse before it, and raise my banner. Resist if you can—come now; if you cannot, be gone.

sentences.zh: 回鶻不能討，其將句錄莫賀導阿熱破殺回鶻可汗，諸特勒皆潰。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs could not suppress him; their general Julu Moho guided A-re to break and kill the Uyghur qaghan, and all the tegins scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs could not crush him. Their general Julu Moho led A-re to rout and kill the Uyghur qaghan; the tegins fled in disarray.

sentences.zh: 阿熱身自將，焚其牙及公主所廬金帳者，回鶻可汗常坐也。

translations.literal: A-re personally commanded, burning the royal camp and the golden tent pavilions of the princess—the seat of the Uyghur qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: A-re took the field himself, burning the royal camp and the princess's golden pavilions—the qaghan's own seat.

sentences.zh: 乃悉收其寶貲，並得太和公主，遂徙牙牢山之南。

translations.literal: He gathered all their treasures and also took Princess Taihe, then moved his headquarters south of Laoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He seized their hoarded wealth and captured Princess Taihe, then shifted his camp south of Laoshan.

sentences.zh: 牢山亦曰賭滿，距回鶻舊牙度馬行十五日。

translations.literal: Laoshan was also called Duman, fifteen days' ride from the old Uyghur camp.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshan—also Duman—lay fifteen days by horse from the former Uyghur headquarters.

sentences.zh: 阿熱以公主唐貴女，遣使者衛送公主還朝，為回鶻烏介可汗邀取之，並殺使者。

translations.literal: Because the princess was a noble woman of Tang, A-re sent envoys to escort her back to court; Uyghur Qaghan Wujie intercepted and seized her, killing the envoys as well.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the princess a woman of Tang rank, A-re sent an escort to return her; Uyghur Qaghan Wujie intercepted the party, took the princess, and slew the envoys.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，阿熱以使者見殺，無以通於朝，復遣註吾合素上書言狀。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era, because envoys had been killed and he had no way to reach the court, he again sent Zhuyu Hesu with a letter stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang, with his envoys slain and no channel to the throne, he sent Zhuyu Hesu with a written account.

sentences.zh: 註吾，虜姓也；

translations.literal: Zhuyu was a barbarian surname;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyu was a foreign clan name;

sentences.zh: 合，言猛；

translations.literal: he, meaning fierce;
translations.idiomatic: he meant "fierce";

sentences.zh: 素者，左也，謂武猛善左射者。

translations.literal: su means left—that is, fierce in battle and skilled with the left hand in archery.
translations.idiomatic: su meant "left"—a warrior fierce in fight and masterful shooting left-handed.

sentences.zh: 行三歲至京師，武宗大悅，班渤海使者上，以其處窮遠，能脩職貢，命太仆卿趙蕃持節臨慰其國，詔宰相即鴻臚寺見使者，使譯官考山川國風。

translations.literal: Three years on the road brought him to the capital; Wuzong was greatly pleased and ranked him above the Bohai envoys. Because his land was remote yet he maintained tribute, Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Fan was ordered as frontier envoy to comfort his state; the emperor commanded the chancellor to receive the envoy at the Honglu Temple and had interpreters examine mountains, rivers, and national customs.
translations.idiomatic: Three years' travel brought him to court. Wuzong rejoiced and seated him above the Bohai embassy. Deeming so distant a land faithful in tribute, he named Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Fan to comfort the realm and ordered the chancellor to meet the envoy at Honglu Temple while interpreters recorded terrain and custom.

sentences.zh: 宰相德裕上言：「貞觀時，遠國皆來，中書侍郎顏師古請如周史臣集四夷朝事為《王會篇》。

translations.literal: Chancellor Deyu memorialized: "In Zhenguan, when distant states all came, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu asked to compile the four barbarians' court audiences after the Zhou historiographer into a 'Assembly of Kings' chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Deyu wrote: "In Zhenguan distant peoples flocked in; Vice Director Yan Shigu proposed a 'Assembly of Kings' chapter after the Zhou model, gathering the four quarters' audiences.

sentences.zh: 今黠戛斯大通中國，宜為《王會圖》以示後世。」

translations.literal: Now that the Kirghiz are thoroughly connected with China, an 'Assembly of Kings' illustration should be made for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Kirghiz are deeply tied to China, we should paint an Assembly of Kings for later ages.

sentences.zh: 有詔以鴻臚所得繢著之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the paintings obtained by Honglu to be used.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Honglu's sketches incorporated.

sentences.zh: 又詔阿熱著宗正屬籍。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered A-re entered on the Directorate of Clans register.
translations.idiomatic: A-re was also entered in the Directorate of Clans registers.

sentences.zh: 是時，烏介可汗餘眾托黑車子，阿熱願乘秋馬肥擊取之，表天子請師。

translations.literal: At that time the remnant of Qaghan Wujie sheltered with the Black Carts; A-re wished to strike them when autumn horses were fat and asked the Son of Heaven for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie's remnant had taken refuge with the Black Carts; A-re asked to attack when autumn horses grew fat and petitioned the throne for soldiers.

sentences.zh: 帝令給事中劉濛為巡邊使，朝廷亦以河、隴四鎮十八州久淪戎狄，幸回鶻破弱，吐蕃亂，相殘嚙，可乘其衰。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Supervising Secretary Liu Meng frontier inspector; the court also noted that the eighteen prefectures of the four He-Long circuits had long lain under barbarian rule, and hoped that with the Uyghurs broken and Tibet in turmoil, mutual devouring might let Tang seize the moment of weakness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Supervising Secretary Liu Meng frontier inspector. The court also noted that eighteen prefectures of the four He-Long commands had long been lost to barbarians; with the Uyghurs crippled and Tibet in chaos, mutual ruin might let Tang recover what was lost.

sentences.zh: 乃以右散騎常侍李拭使黠戛斯，冊君長為宗英雄武誠明可汗。

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant of the Crown Li Shi was then sent to the Kirghiz to invest the ruler as Qaghan Zongying Xiongwu Chengming.
translations.idiomatic: Right Regular Attendant Li Shi was dispatched to invest the Kirghiz ruler as Qaghan Zongying Xiongwu Chengming.

sentences.zh: 未行，而武宗崩。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Wuzong died.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet departed when Wuzong died.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嗣位，欲如先帝意，或謂黠戛斯小種，不足與唐抗，詔宰相與臺省四品以上官議，皆曰：「回鶻盛時有冊號，今幸衰亡，又加黠戛斯，後且生患。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong succeeded and wished to follow the late emperor's intent, but some said the Kirghiz were a petty tribe unfit to stand as Tang's equal; the emperor ordered the chancellor and officials of fourth rank and above in the Secretariat and Censorate to deliberate. All said: "When the Uyghurs were strong they bore investiture; now that they have fallen, to add the Kirghiz will breed trouble hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong wished to honor his predecessor's plan, but critics called the Kirghiz a minor people unworthy of Tang parity. He convened the chancellor and Secretariat and Censorate officials of the fourth rank and above; all argued: "The Uyghurs at their height received titles; now that they are ruined, elevating the Kirghiz will only breed future harm.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 至大中元年，卒詔鴻臚卿李業持節冊黠戛斯為英武誠明可汗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong an edict was at last issued: Minister of Honglu Li Ye was sent with credentials to invest the Kirghiz as Qaghan Yingwu Chengming.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 1 Li Ye, Minister of Honglu, was finally sent to invest the Kirghiz as Qaghan Yingwu Chengming.

sentences.zh: 逮咸通間，三來朝。

translations.literal: By the Xiantong period they came to court three times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiantong they presented themselves three times.

sentences.zh: 然卒不能取回鶻。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they could not destroy the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: They never succeeded in finishing off the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 後之朝聘冊命，史臣失傳。

translations.literal: Later court audiences, investiture, and commands—the historians lost the record.
translations.idiomatic: Later embassies, titles, and edicts went unrecorded by the historians.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：夷狄資悍貪，人外而獸內，惟剽奪是視。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Barbarians by nature rely on fierceness and greed; outwardly men, inwardly beasts—they see only plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Barbarians are fierce and greedy by nature—human in face, beast at heart—seeing nothing but raid and spoil.

sentences.zh: 故湯、武之興，未嘗與共功，蓋疏而不戚也。

translations.literal: Hence when Tang and Wu rose they never shared achievement with them, keeping them at distance without intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang of Shang and King Wu rose, they never made barbarians partners in founding the state, keeping them distant and without close kinship.

sentences.zh: 太宗初興，嘗用突厥矣，不勝其暴，卒縛而臣之。

translations.literal: When Taizong first rose he once employed the Turks but could not bear their violence and in the end bound and made them subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong at the start of his reign used the Turks, could not endure their brutality, and finally bound them into submission.

sentences.zh: 肅宗用回紇矣，至略華人，辱太子，笞殺近臣，求索無倪。

translations.literal: Suzong employed the Huihe, who came to plunder Chinese lands, insult the crown prince, beat and kill courtiers close at hand, and demand without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong turned to the Huihe, who ravaged Chinese territory, humiliated the crown prince, flogged and killed nearby officials, and exacted without end.

sentences.zh: 德宗又用吐蕃矣，劫平涼，敗上將，空破西陲。

translations.literal: Dezong employed the Tibetans, who raided Pingliang, defeated a chief general, and emptied the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong relied on Tibet, which struck Pingliang, routed a leading general, and gutted the western border.

sentences.zh: 所謂引外禍平內亂者也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by inviting foreign calamity to quell internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the meaning of inviting foreign disaster to settle domestic turmoil.

sentences.zh: 夫用之以權，制之以謀，惟太宗能之。

translations.literal: To employ them by expedient and control them by stratagem—only Taizong could do this.
translations.idiomatic: Using them when useful and restraining them by design—only Taizong mastered that art.

sentences.zh: 若二主懦昏，狃而狎之，烏勝其弊哉！

translations.literal: When two emperors were weak and benighted, clinging to barbarians and treating them familiarly, how could harm be avoided!
translations.idiomatic: But when two rulers were timid and dim, clinging to barbarians and handling them lightly, what ruin could be avoided!

sentences.zh: 彼親之則責償也多，慊而不滿則滋怨，化以仁義則頑，示以法則忿，熟我險易則為患也博而慘，療餒以冶葛，何時可哉？

translations.literal: Those treated as kin demand heavy repayment; when desire is unsated resentment grows. Civilize them with benevolence and righteousness and they remain stubborn; show them law and they rage. Once they know our terrain they bring broader, crueller harm. To feed hunger with monkshood poison—when will that end?
translations.idiomatic: Favor breeds endless claims; unmet appetite breeds hate. Benevolence and righteousness leave them unchanged; law only angers them. Learn our passes and rivers and their harm grows wider and bloodier. Healing famine with monkshood—is there an end?

sentences.zh: 故《春秋》許夷狄者，不一而足，信矣。

translations.literal: Hence the Spring and Autumn Annals rarely approves the barbarians—and rightly so.
translations.idiomatic: So the Spring and Autumn rarely praises the barbarians—and how true that is.
